stories.title: Sources: Warriors exploring options to trade center Kristaps Porzingis
stories.summary: The Warriors have begun exploring trade routes for veteran center Kristaps Porzingis, who remains out indefinitely as he deals with a private health issue, league sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.
stories.detailText: The Golden State Warriors have begun exploring trade routes for veteran center Kristaps Porzingis , who remains out indefinitely as he deals with a private health issue that has him seriously contemplating his future in basketball, league sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. The Warriors released a statement Wednesday saying they were "not going to comment on trade speculation or reports regarding his health-related matter or future." Porzingis signed a two-year, $40 million extension with the team in June, but only $3 million of the $20 million in the second season is guaranteed, essentially making it an expiring contract. The front office strategically designed the extension without a raise between the two seasons, keeping him immediately trade-eligible instead of needing to wait until mid-December. Despite the built-in flexibility, that wasn't the idealized intent of the contract. Porzingis played in 15 of the team's final 20 games last season, and the Warriors' management believed he had an encouraging enough summer to pencil Porzingis in as the projected starting center next to Draymond Green and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg in the frontcourt. Porzingis was in the team's San Francisco facility and on the court in the week leading up to training camp. And he attended Jimmy Butler 's player-led event in San Diego in late September, though team sources described a detached Porzingis as indifferent and uninterested in participating in scrimmages and strenuous on-court prep work at the event. On the Sunday before training camp, Porzingis called the Warriors and alerted general manager Mike Dunleavy that he was still dealing with the lingering impact of a health issue that has bothered him for nearly two years and said he would be taking an indefinite leave of absence . Two seasons ago, Porzingis contracted an upper respiratory virus while playing for the Boston Celtics , and he has since vaguely revealed the lingering impact it has had on his energy level and ability to consistently play NBA basketball. Porzingis has termed it a POTS (postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome) diagnosis, which can lead to bouts of dizziness, fatigue and brain fog. After missing the first two weeks of training camp and the entire preseason, Porzingis drove up from Los Angeles to San Francisco last Tuesday, league sources said, to meet with Dunleavy and Rick Celebrini, the franchise's lead medical decision-maker. In the aftermath, the team announced that they would keep the details of the meeting private, but expressed an expectation that Porzingis would remain around the team as he tried to improve his health and eventually resume his career. But that hasn't been the case. Porzingis hasn't returned to the facility, league sources said, beginning another indefinite leave of absence where he is mostly maintaining contact with only Dunleavy and Celebrini. The Warriors listed him as out for the season opener against the Los Angeles Lakers on Wednesday night and the reasoning as "not with team" instead of an illness. "As noted last week, conversations between the Warriors, Kristaps, and his representatives will remain private," Wednesday's statement by the Warriors said. "We are not anticipating Kristaps being around the team in the immediate future. We'll provide additional updates when available and appropriate." If there is no breakthrough with Porzingis' recovery, stepping away from basketball -- for good -- is possible for him, sources told Charania. "It has definitely been frustrating dealing with some health stuff that you can't exactly pinpoint, on top of injuries throughout my career," Porzingis wrote in an X post last week . "So it has added up for sure, but we will get through it." It's unclear what type of trade market Porzingis' contract would have at the onset of the regular season. Most front offices are generally intent on finding out what they have with their current mix before exploring larger shake-ups, but draft assets can always entice even without a guarantee Porzingis will return to an NBA court. The Warriors still have a nearly full cupboard of first-rounders and several expiring contracts. Dunleavy has made it clear in his public statements that part of the team's roster build this season allowed for an in-season trade strike if the right deal can be found.

stories.title: Sources: Mavericks agree to two-way deal with Walter Clayton Jr.
stories.summary: The Mavericks agree to a two-way NBA deal with former first-round pick Walter Clayton Jr., sources told ESPN.
stories.detailText: The Dallas Mavericks have agreed on a two-way NBA deal with former first-round pick Walter Clayton Jr., sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Wednesday. Clayton was waived earlier this week by the Memphis Grizzlies ahead of the league's roster cut-down deadline. He is joining the Mavericks after clearing waivers. Memphis acquired Clayton from Utah on Feb. 3 in the eight-player trade that sent Jaren Jackson Jr ., Jock Landale , John Konchar and Vince Williams Jr. to the Jazz. Clayton played 24 games for the Grizzlies last season after the trade, averaging 9.7 points, 2.1 rebounds and 5.7 assists and shooting 36.6% from 3-point range. Clayton, 23, was the No. 18 pick in the 2025 draft after helping Florida win its third national title. He was named the Final Four's Most Outstanding Player and was a consensus first-team All-American in 2025. The Mavericks, still light on ball handlers despite the return of Kyrie Irving from his ACL injury, could use the depth Clayton provides in their backcourt.

First, Golden State is hard capped at the second apron and isn't allowed to take back more salary than what is sent out. Oct. 16 Marks: A busy weekend of transaction expected The last weekend of the offseason is expected to bring a flurry of transactions. Starting on Saturday Oct. 17, teams will need to decide on players signed to non-guaranteed contracts. If a player is on the roster past 5 p.m. ET, teams will begin incurring a per day salary charge. For example, the New York Knicks would be charged $17,622 per day against the cap if James Wiseman is not waived by Saturday. However, despite a mandate to remain under the second apron, New York is allowed to keep Wiseman and Bruce Brown to start the season. The deadline for rookie extensions is Monday by 6 p.m. ET. Since the start of the offseason, five players -- Victor Wembanyama , Amen and Ausar Thompson , Keyonte George and Brandin Podziemski -- have signed rookie extensions. The 2023 rookie class of extended players are below the per year average of 11 players we have seen since 2023. Some of the notable names to watch include Brandon Miller and Cason Wallace . Keep in mind that out of the 34 players who signed rookie extensions in the prior three seasons, 17 came on the last day of eligibility. The rookie extension deadline is not the only date teams are paying attention to, however. Oct. 19 is also the deadline to extend veterans who have two years left on their contract -- not including an option year -- and the last day to reduce rosters to 15 players on standard contracts. -- Bobby Marks Read more: Which NBA deals will get done? stories.title: The Warriors’ terrible Kristaps Porzingis news is a problem without a viable solution
stories.summary: Kristaps Porzingis’ diagnosis is terrible news for the Warriors.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Would you believe that Kristaps Porzingis graded out as one of the better players in the NBA last season? It’s true. Porzingis ranked No. 50 in the league in Estimated Plus-Minus and nearly cracked the top-25 in LEBRON, which are a pair of metrics that measure a player’s impact with some luck adjustments and player tracking data built in . Every all-in-one stat is going to have blindspots and needs to be taken with a large grain of salt, but both teams Porzingis played for last season — the Atlanta Hawks and Golden State Warriors — were much better with him on the court in his 32 total games, and that’s no coincidence. Porzingis showed the whole world how good he could be on the Boston Celtics’ run to the 2024 NBA championship, when his combination of outside shooting and rim protection made him the rare center who could space the floor to the max without giving much back on defense. Porzingis’ effectiveness hasn’t been much of a question since his career-defining season in Boston, but his availability has been. Unfortunately, Porzingis remains out for the Warriors as they begin the 2026-27 season, and now the team appears ready to move on without him. The Warriors are exploring trade packages for Porzingis as he deals with POTS (Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome), a nervous system disorder that causes dizziness, brain fog, chronic fatigue, and other unwanted symptoms. Porzingis is “contemplating his future in basketball” according to ESPN insider Shams Charania . Speculation on Porzingis’ rampant health problems dating back to the Celtics’ 2024 playoff run had grown so out of control that the 31-year-old felt obligated to put out a pair of statements clarifying that doesn’t have AIDS or HIV last week. Now his NBA career might be over as the Warriors scramble for a backup plan. Hello people, I'm working with doctors and experts to figure out how to be fully back to good health asap. Honestly, I'm getting better and better. I just have to stay patient, and I believe I'll be feeling great again soon. It has definitely been frustrating dealing with some… — Kristaps Porzingis (@kporzee) October 14, 2026 I appreciate all the internet doctors trying to diagnose and help, but I'm in the best hands. So everyone can relax now 😄🙏🏼 and I don’t have hiv or aids. — Kristaps Porzingis (@kporzee) October 14, 2026 The biggest story here is the premature end of Porzingis’ career for health problems entirely out of his control. It’s an incredibly sad development for such a talented player who had so much promise early in his career, and appeared to find renewed value after being dumped to the Washington Wizards in 2022. This is also deeply disappointing news for the Warriors, because it’s going to be tough to find another player who can approximate his skill set without adding the type of valuable future assets Golden State has resisted including in other deals. What team would trade for a player who might be finished? Porzingis’ contract could still make him valuable around the league depending on a few factors. He only has $3 million guaranteed for next season, but counts for $20 million in a trade. If another team was looking to dump a player they don’t want around anymore with long-term money on the books, they might be incentivized to trade for Porzingis and then just cut him while stomaching the $3 million next season. Let’s say the Milwaukee Bucks decide that they just want Myles Turner off the books as he enters the second season of a four-year, $109 million deal. The Warriors could take Turner, the Bucks could take Porzingis, and then Milwaukee could waive him to save some money. The Chicago Bulls could build a similar trade around Patrick Williams, who has three years remaining on his contract as this season begins. The Turner idea in particular could sound good in theory, but it takes two sides to make a deal, and the Warriors don’t have much leverage. Golden State’s only real backup center is Al Horford, who is 40 years old. Charles Bassey is around too, but he’s never been counted on for more than a small role. Losing Quentin Post to the Memphis Grizzlies over the summer in free agency was a tough blow, and now the Warriors seem like they’re totally out of options in the front court unless they want to part with a meaningful asset. Warriors lead executive Mike Dunleavy is already on the record saying fixing the team’s center problem is “not as simple as hey, let’s go find someone new” with 15 players already on the roster. Golden State is already without Jimmy Butler as he recovers from a torn ACL, and Moses Moody as he tries to come back from a ruptured patellar tendon. That’s $90 million in salary not in the lineup to start the year. This is no way to build around Stephen Curry in his age-38 season. Rookie forward Yaxel Lendeborg looks amazing , but it’s hard to win without a reliable center, and the Warriors are being immediately put in a compromising position. This is a bummer of a story. Let’s hope Porzingis can find peace after basketball if this really is it for his career.

stories.title: Golden State Warriors reportedly consider Kristaps Porzingis trade
stories.summary: Golden State Warriors are reportedly looking to trade center Kristaps Porzingis as health concerns grow. Here are the latest updates.
stories.detailText: Editor's note: This story has been updated to include a statement from the Golden State Warriors . The Golden State Warriors have grown increasingly concerned about Kristaps Porzingis's availability and are exploring other options for the 31-year-old center, according to a new report. Golden State has begun to search for trade partners to part ways with Porzingis , according to ESPN. Porzingis is reportedly contemplating his basketball future as he continues to deal with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) autoimmune symptoms. USA TODAY Sports reached out to the team, but the Warriors were not available to comment on the matter. The team did, however, release a statement on the matter. "In response to today’s media report regarding Kristaps Porzingis, we are not going to comment on trade speculation or reports regarding his health-related matter or future," the Warriors statement read Wednesday afternoon. "As noted last week, conversations between the Warriors, Kristaps and his representatives will remain private. We are not anticipating Kristaps being around the team in the immediate future. We’ll provide additional updates when available and appropriate." Head coach Steve Kerr told reporters after practice Tuesday that he and Porzingis spoke recently, exchanging phone calls "a couple days ago" and text messages throughout the last couple of weeks. "Other than my concern for him and his own well-being, I don't think of it," Kerr said when asked how he's handling the situation. "When we come to practice, I don't think of it because I have to focus on the guys who are here. That's my concern." "When we come into the building, it's 'how are we going to play? How are we going to start? Who's going to back up the 5s? If Al (Horford) doesn't play, does (Ike) Graham play? Do we use one of the two-way games that he has? Those are all the basketball thoughts," Kerr added. "But as I've mentioned to you guys out first order of business is to support Kristaps and help him through this." Kristaps Porzingis latest injury updates Last week, Porzingis met with general manager Mike Dunleavy and Rick Celebrini , vice president of player health and performance, after previously being away from the team with an undisclosed illness. The team said the details of that meeting would "remain private," but Porzingis posted on X (formerly Twitter) that he was working with medical professionals to figure out how to get back to full health. "I'm working with doctors and experts to figure out how to be fully back to good health asap. Honestly, I'm getting better and better. I just have to stay patient, and I believe I'll be feeling great again soon," Porzingis wrote. "It has definitely been frustrating dealing with some health stuff that you can't exactly pinpoint, on top of injuries throughout my career, so it has added up for sure, but we will get through it. Health is wealth. Thank you for all the support at the Warriors practice facility" He's heard the jokes and seen the Internet trolls who have had think-pieces about Porzingis's health. "I appreciate all the internet doctors trying to diagnose and help, but I'm in the best hands," Porzingis wrote on social media. "So everyone can relax now and I don’t have HIV or Aids." This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Golden State Warriors reportedly consider Kristaps Porzingis trade

stories.detailText: The Golden State Warriors have begun exploring trades of center Kristaps Porziņģis, who remains away from the team and is "seriously contemplating his future in basketball," ESPN’s Shams Charania reports . Porziņģis has been away from the Warriors since before training camp, and Charania's report confirms he is still dealing with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome, or POTS. People with this condition see their heart rate race for a minute or more after standing up from sitting or lying down (as part of the disorder, more blood stays in your lower body even after a person stands, causing the heart rate to race as it tries to get blood flowing again). This condition has limited Porziņģis' ability to play for a couple of seasons. Porziņģis signed a two-year, $40 million contract extension with the Warriors last offseason, but only $3 million of the 2027-28 season is guaranteed, essentially making him an expiring contract. Golden State is looking into packaging Porzingis (mostly as salary ballast) with players or picks to bring in someone of value in a trade. Teams that acquire Porziņģis would very likely waive him next summer, as they'd get the financial savings plus the real draw of whatever the Warriors add to the trade package. Porziņģis came into the Warriors' practice facility last week to discuss his situation with team doctors and management. Afterward, he posted this on X. I appreciate all the internet doctors trying to diagnose and help, but I'm in the best hands. So everyone can relax now and I don’t have hiv or aids. — Kristaps Porzingis (@kporzee) October 14, 2026 Golden State acquired Porziņģis at last year's trade deadline, envisioning him as a stretch big who can protect the rim and fit very well next to Stephen Curry. Porziņģis played in 15 games for Golden State last season and averaged 16.1 points, 5.3 rebounds and 1.1 blocks per game. Based on that, the Warriors bet on Porziņģis this summer and gave him an extension.

stories.title: Luka Dončić takes out full-page ad in LA Times ahead of Lakers season-opener Wednesday night
stories.summary: Dončić is heading into his second full season with L.A.
stories.detailText: The Los Angeles Lakers open the 2026-27 season at home on Wednesday night against the Golden State Warriors. Ahead of the game, star guard Luka Dončić took out a full-page ad in the LA Times and wrote a message to the Lakers faithful. "Tonight we start our run for a championship. Every player dreams of holding that trophy. To do it for all you amazing fans would mean everything to us. Each of us understands what it means to put on this purple and gold jersey and follow the players who wore it before us. It means so much because of the passion and dedication that generations of you all have shown for this team. I see it everywhere. The hats, the flags on cars, the murals. This city has people from all over the world, speaking every language, and the Lakers are the thing that brings everyone together. We have a special team. We know what you expect, and we are going to do everything in our power to deliver it. From the moment I arrived in L.A., you welcomed me with open arms. That is something I will never forget. So here is my promise to you: we are going to give you everything we have, every single night. No excuses. No nights off. But we cannot do this alone. You are the best fans in the world, and we are going to need you. Every game, bring it with us. Let's go. " “Tonight we start our run for a championship.” 🏆 Luka Doncic took out a full-page ad in the LA Times ahead of the Lakers’ home opener 💜💛 pic.twitter.com/vYSQv6ThcM — Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) October 21, 2026 Dončić is heading into his second full season with Los Angeles. He joined the Lakers ahead of the 2025 trade deadline in the infamous deal that sent him from the Dallas Mavericks to the Lakers overnight. Last year, Dončić played 64 games for the Lakers, the most in a season since 2023-24. He averaged 33.5 points, 7.7 rebounds and 8.3 assists per game. It was the second-highest points-per-game mark of his career. This marks a new era for Los Angeles, with Dončić as the team's focal point. It will be the first season since 2018 that the Lakers won't have LeBron James on the roster, as the future Hall of Famer signed with the Philadelphia 76ers in free agency this offseason. Dončić's statement shows he knows his role now and what fans still expect from the franchise, even without James in town. The guard's first chance to back up his words comes in Wednesday night's season opener.

In five games, the Los Angeles Lakers guard averaged 2.2 points, 2.8 assists and 2.4 rebounds while playing 16.4 minutes each night. He committed 12 turnovers and shot 25% from the floor and 12.5% beyond the arc. It was certainly not the sort of production that would endear James to anyone as he vies for a slim chance at rotation minutes to begin the year. His head coach, JJ Redick, even acknowledged James’ slow preseason . But according to a report from ESPN’s Dave McMenamin , James has not been fully healthy and Redick believes he hasn’t always been put in situations most conducive to success during training camp. “James, for his part, has been limited by a quad contusion he suffered just before the start of training camp, sources told ESPN,“ McMenamin wrote, ”and Redick added that the third-year guard has often shared the court with training camp invitees, rather than rotation players and noted how James finished last season as a playoff contributor.“ The Lakers presumably will not be counting on James for crucial minutes to open 2026-27 or whenever they’re mostly healthy. But James did occasionally crack the rotation last season and Redick’s previously harped on the important of back-end bench guys to step up when others are unavailable. He and the entire Lakers organization will hope James’ quad contusion was the catalyst for his poor preseason and that he’ll be able to offer solid minutes if called upon. Ahead of James in the guard room are the likes of Austin Reaves, Luka Dončić (if he counts), Collin Sexton, Quentin Grimes and Matisse Thybulle, though I suspect the latter two here will see their fair share of minutes on the wings. Others such as Jaden Hardy, Chris Mañon and rookie Cameron Carr will duke it out with James for spot minutes in the backcourt. When in form, James’ on-ball defense, shooting (38.6% from 3 last year) and connective passing can be of use. But he’ll have to prove last year was not an aberration beyond the arc and that he’s at least a mild threat with the ball in his hands, which has been a struggle throughout his career. stories.title: A letter to Suns Nation: 2026-27 Season Edition
stories.summary: Can the Suns build off a surprising 2025-26 campaign?
stories.detailText: PHOENIX, ARIZONA - MARCH 08: Devin Booker #1 of the Phoenix Suns celebrates with Collin Gillespie #12 after scoring against the Charlotte Hornets during the second half of the NBA game at Mortgage Matchup Center on March 08, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. The Suns defeated the Hornets 111-99. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Dear Phoenix Suns Nation, A year ago, if someone had told you that coming into this season, the Suns would be looking to build off a 45-win season and a playoff appearance, what would you have said? Your response and perspective may dictate how you feel about this season. Whether it’s the 2022 New York Giants, who made the NFC divisional round and haven’t returned to the playoffs since, or the Sacramento Kings back in 2023, who were the Western Conference’s third seed and have been at the bottom of the standings ever since, just because a team has a surprising season doesn’t mean that the following one is just as successful. But it also doesn’t mean that expectations should be dimmed by the surprise of the previous season. Based on their continuity, offseason acquisitions, and internal development, the Suns should be a better team than they were a season ago, pending health, of course. The team has brought back an overwhelming majority of its key players in a conference that saw a lot of turnover from a season ago. LeBron James is in the city of brotherly love, Kawhi Leonard is in Canada, and the Minnesota Timberwolves and Los Angeles Lakers’ starting lineups are vastly different from what they were a season ago. With Jalen Green healthy to start the year, unlike a season ago, the team is looking at their season-long starting lineup set to be mostly the same from game 1 to game 82, once they decide whether Khaman Maluach or Oso Ighodaro will be the team’s starting center. The only new starter on the team? While there are numerous questions about him off the court, he should be a significant upgrade over Royce O’Neale at the starting power forward spot because of Bridges’ ability to create his own shot and experience playing alongside ball-dominant guards. Luke Kennard, who is set to replace Grayson Allen, is coming off the best playoff performances of his career and is one of the NBA’s best three-point shooters. Expect Phoenix to jack up a lot of triples this year. Collin Gillespie, Dillon Brooks, Jordan Goodwin, and Oso Ighodaro? All back in Suns uniforms, with new contracts. Along with Mark Williams as well, but he should be out for the majority of the season, dealing with a shoulder injury he suffered in the offseason. The extensions and re-signings of key members of the team’s core from a season ago add stability that should provide the team and players more confidence to grow on their strong seasons while in the early or middle primes of their careers. The Western Conference, however, is deeper than it was a season ago. Even if the Suns are a better team than they were a year ago, it might not translate to more wins. The top eight in the Western Conference all made moves to stay competitive, but the teams in the bottom half of the standings have either made moves or are getting players back from injury that should make them more formidable. The anti-tanking rules, along with the 2026 draft class projected to be one of the most star-studded in recent memory, have raised the floor of many of the conference’s worst teams from last season. The incentives to bottom out and lose as much as possible are gone, and teams in the conference have responded. The Utah Jazz, who selected Kansas’ Darryn Peterson second overall in the draft and traded for former Defensive Player of the Year Jaren Jackson Jr. back in February, are expected to take a leap this year despite losing young center Walker Kessler to the Lakers in free agency. The Memphis Grizzlies, albeit a young team, are expected to make some noise after taking who many executives believe is the most NBA-ready prospect in Cam Boozer. And the Dallas Mavericks, who were without All-Star guard Kyrie Irving for the entirety of the 2025-26 season, should be vastly improved from last year with Cooper Flagg a year older and the team another season removed from the disastrous Luke Dončić trade. The Suns might be better than they were a season ago. They might not have the drop-offs that the Kings and Giants mean, and it might mean that they’re out of the playoffs again, let alone the play-in tournament. But if you can remember just 365 days ago when the idea of the Suns playing in the playoffs sounded as likely as the Cowboys in the Super Bowl, then maybe it’ll be easier to deal with whatever the 2026-2027 season has in store. No matter good or bad, like every season, it’ll be an entertaining one. It’s NBA basketball. Sincerely, Holden Sherman

stories.title: Victor Wembanyama on opening night struggles vs. Thunder: "I might be overthinking it"
stories.summary: "What I have to do is really let go. I don't need to do more. I need to think less, probably."
stories.detailText: Unsurprisingly, Victor Wembanyama didn't have fun during the Spurs' opening-season loss to the Thunder. He started the game by missing his first 12 shots, and while he had six blocked shots and impacted the game in other ways, he was the key reason San Antonio started the season 0-1. After the game, the introspective Wembanyama essentially said he has to stop thinking so much. "I need to go back to playing the basketball I like. This is not the sport I like, right here," Wembanyama said. "I got no reason to be hesitant, no reason to not be myself. For me, it's as simple as that. I'm good when I have fun... "I missed lots of lots of shots, which I usually don't miss. But after that, I didn't go back to these shots. I wasn't decisive. I might be overthinking it, and I feel like it's a chance for me. What I have to do is really let go. I don't need to do more. I need to think less, probably." Was part of his overthinking it the adjustment to new spacing — less of it — with the three-guard De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper lineups? "I would say we haven't been good enough to find that out," Wembanyama said. Part of that also is that the Spurs were playing the Thunder, the best defensive team in the NBA last season and one of the few teams with the depth and size to throw multiple 7-footers at Wembanyama to be physical with him. OKC is also loaded with quality perimeter defenders who made life tough for the Spurs trio of guards. Wembanyama still made his presence felt with six blocks, fantastic overall defense and 13 rebounds. Victor Wembanyama was flying all over the court and was wreaking havoc! pic.twitter.com/LMlV2NxY5w — NBA on NBC and Peacock (@NBAonNBC) October 21, 2026 Wembanyama, at 22, is a thoughtful, high-IQ player, but he would be far from the first great player to suffer "paralysis through analysis." When Wembanyama is playing his best, there is a flow to what he is doing, it happens naturally, instinctively. If the Spurs are going back to the NBA Finals, they need more out of Wembanyama — and specifically more against the Thunder. This was just one of 82, there is a long road ahead, but Wemby understands he has to get back to being himself, to having fun, or that road will seem even longer.

You are the best fans in the world, and we are going to need you. Every game, bring it with us. Let’s go. During his days with the Dallas Mavericks, Dončić embedded himself in the Dallas community. When wildfires devastated parts of Los Angeles in 2025, Dončić, shortly after being traded to the Lakers, donated $500,000 through the Luka Dončić Foundation . When Dončić learned of a GoFundMe campaign to help restore a vandalized mural of Kobe and Gianna Bryant in April 2025, he met the $5,000 fundraiser goal himself . On other occasions, he’s helped enhance game-day experiences for fans . Wednesday’s ad is yet another example of Dončić connecting with the Lakers fanbase and showcasing his commitment to being the face of the franchise. Because of the attention and hype surrounding Dončić‘s entrance to the NBA 8.5 years ago, much has been expected of him for many years. And because of how well he’s played, earning six All-NBA nods and four top-five MVP finishes, much has continued to be expected of him. Of course, those expectations largely revolve around his on-court play. But a superstar of Dončić’s magnitude is often required to stretch their scope beyond in-game performance. Dončić clearly understands and embraces his responsibilities. No matter which city and franchise he’s called home, he’s been a mainstay in the community and sought to better the lives of his supporters in some capacity. Now, it’s time to see whether this team is ready to reach the championship aspirations Dončić has laid out. You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .

stories.title: Kristaps Porziņģis weighing NBA future amid recurring health condition, Warriors exploring trades: report
stories.summary: Porziņģis was first diagnosed with POTS in 2025.
stories.detailText: The Golden State Warriors are exploring trade options involving forward Kristaps Porziņģis, ESPN's Shams Charania reports . Porziņģis has been away from the team while dealing with recurring POTS (Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome) symptoms. Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season Last week, the Warriors forward posted on social media about his health. "Hello people, I'm working with doctors and experts to figure out how to be fully back to good health asap," the one-time All-Star and NBA champion wrote . "Honestly, I'm getting better and better. I just have to stay patient, and I believe I'll be feeling great again soon. It has definitely been frustrating dealing with some health stuff that you can't exactly pinpoint, on top of injuries throughout my career, so it has added up for sure, but we will get through it. "Health is wealth. Thank you for all the support." Porziņģis also added: "I appreciate all the internet doctors trying to diagnose and help, but I'm in the best hands. So everyone can relax now … and I don't have hiv or aids." The Warriors’ acknoweldged the report on Wednesday, but said in a statement that they wouldn’t comment on either trade speculation or reports on Porzingis’ health and future. “As noted last week, conversations between the Warriors, Kristaps and his rperesentatives will remain private,” the team said . “We are not anticipating Kristaps being around the team in teh immediate future.” On Oct. 14, before Porziņģis released his statement, Golden State announced the forward would remain " out indefinitely " and, at the time, called it a "health-related" matter. Charania's Wednesday report was the first time it was said to be recurring POTS symptoms, and that the forward was contemplating his future in the sport. Porziņģis was first diagnosed with POTS in 2025. According to Cleveland Clinic , "POTS is a condition that causes your heart to beat faster than normal when you go from sitting or lying down to standing up." Symptoms can vary widely from patient to patient, but Porziņģis' seem more respiratory and fatigue-related. POTS significantly limited the 7-foot-2 Porziņģis during an Eastern Conference semifinal series against the New York Knicks in the 2024-25 season, when he was still with the Boston Celtics. Porziņģis averaged just 15.5 minutes in that six-game series, which ended Boston's NBA title defense, with Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla revealing after Game 5 that Porziņģis didn't play the second half because " he couldn't breathe ." The Knicks selected Porziņģis with the fourth overall pick in the 2015 NBA Draft. He previously played overseas for Sevilla in Spain. Porziņģis spent three seasons with the Knicks before missing the entire 2018-19 season with a torn ACL. He then bounced around the league, spending time with the Dallas Mavericks, Washington Wizards, Celtics, Atlanta Hawks and Warriors. Over his 10-year career, Porziņģis has played 533 games. He is averaging 19.5 points, 7.6 rebounds, and 1.9 assists per game. Last year, the forward split his time between the Hawks and the Warriors. Overall, he played in 32 games and averaged 16.7 points, 5.2 rebounds, and 2.5 assists per game. It was the fewest games he played in a season in his career, outside of the missed 2018-19 campaign, and his lowest points-per-game average since his rookie season in 2015-16.

stories.title: Rangers See What Championship Success Means To New York Through Knicks
stories.summary: As the New York Knicks raised their championship banner on Tuesday night, some members of the New York Rangers were at Madison Square Garden to witness the historic moment.
stories.detailText: Brad Penner-Imagn Images As the New York Knicks raised their championship banner on Tuesday night, some members of the New York Rangers were at Madison Square Garden to witness the historic moment. In June, the Knicks won their first championship in 53 years, bringing a joyful energy and uniting the entire city of New York. Sharing a practice facility and both playing at The World’s Most Famous Arena, the Rangers and Knicks are bonded together under the MSG umbrella. For the Rangers, witnessing the Knicks win a championship and seeing the impact it had on the city was something the whole organization took to heart. “It’s inspiring,” Mike Sullivan said. “It’s inspiring when a group has witnessed the ultimate success in their respective sport. When it’s close to you, these guys, we have lunch with the Knicks a lot, so there’s some familiarity. I know both teams root for one another. We couldn’t be more proud of them and I think a night like last night is inspiring for our guys, Noah Laba, Gabe Perreault, Will Cuylle, Alexis Lafrenière, Vladislav Gavrikov, Sean Durzi, and Eeli Tolvanen were all in attendance for the Knicks’ opening-night game on Tuesday night, in which the team received their championship rings and raised the championship banner. “It was great,” Vladislav Gavrikov said about attending the Knicks game. “The atmosphere, the building was electric. Those moments that they showed on the jumbotron, the video and everything, you are getting goosebumps to that. Obviously, that was a special night.” The Rangers got a taste of what it could be like to be a champion in New York by watching the Knicks this summer and now further realize the magnitude sports has on the city. “I think we saw it all summer, the parade and just all of the streets,” Perreault said of the Knicks’ championship win. “It shows you the fan base in New York and obviously if we could do that one day, it would be super cool.”

stories.title: The King of Cool: P&T’s interview with Walt “Clyde” Frazier
stories.summary: Clyde reads Posting & Toasting!
stories.detailText: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - JUNE 08: Former New York Knicks player Walt Frazier poses prior to Game Three between the New York Knicks and the San Antonio Spurs in the 2026 NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden on June 08, 2026 in New York City. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Dustin Satloff/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you were to look up the words cool , stylish , flair , and all-time great in the dictionary, you would find four distinct definitions, each describing a quality that few individuals can truly embody. Cool: Very fashionable, impressive, or appealing in a way that is universally admired. Stylish: Possessing a high degree of quality in appearance, design, or behavior. Flair: A natural talent or ability to do things in an original, stylish, and captivating manner. All-Time Great: An individual regarded among the very best to ever perform in a particular field, sport, or profession. What’s missing alongside each of these definitions in the dictionary is a picture of Walt “Clyde” Frazier. Throughout the storied history of the NBA, countless legends have left their mark on the game, but few, if any, have embodied all four qualities quite like Frazier. From his legendary playing days with the New York Knicks in the 1970s to his continued presence as one of the most recognizable personalities in basketball more than five decades later, Frazier remains in a class of his own, both on and off the court. A man whose legendary style extends far beyond his flamboyant wardrobe, Frazier helped define an era of New York basketball, captivating fans with his effortless cool, unparalleled court vision, tenacious defense, and undeniable flair. Widely regarded as one of the greatest players in New York Knicks franchise history, Frazier’s place among basketball royalty is unquestionable. A two-time NBA champion, seven-time NBA All-Star, and member of both the NBA’s 50th and 75th Anniversary Teams, his legacy is as timeless as the city he helped bring to basketball prominence. Simply put, there has never been another Walt “Clyde” Frazier. And chances are, there never will be. Let’s start with his style. Clyde’s style was unlike anybody else’s in the NBA during the ‘70s, and to this day, there still hasn’t been a close second. As a young man in his twenties, Frazier became just as recognizable for driving around New York City in his custom Rolls-Royce while sporting a full-length mink coat and fedora as he was for his play on the court. Today, his fashion sense remains as distinctive as ever. Throughout a broadcasting career spanning nearly 40 years, including almost 30 as a television commentator for MSG and the Knicks, his wardrobe has remained unmistakable, from tiger-print suits to custom blazers reminiscent of Joseph’s Technicolor Dreamcoat. There arguably hasn’t been a more fashionable icon in the NBA’s nearly 80-year history. (Original Caption) NEW YORK: Apparently determined to match his flashy drives on the basketball court with some equally flashy driving, New York Knicks' star guard Walt Frazier gets set for a spin in his sleek Rolls Royce. For the fourth straight year, Frazier was named Jan. 9 as a starter on the East team in the NBA all-star game to be played in Chicago Jan. 23. Frazier was a trendsetter, one of the first NBA players to truly express his personality through his wardrobe, at a time when players were largely known for what they did on the court rather than what they wore off it. His style became a part of his identity, both during his playing days and throughout his broadcasting career, setting him apart from his contemporaries and the generations of NBA stars who followed. So, just how did Walt Frazier become Clyde? “Coming to the Mecca. New York City. Fashion, passion,” Frazier explains. “When we played, we wore suits and ties to the game. We were always trying to outdress each other. Our idols were The Temptations, The Four Tops. So we emulated the way these guys performed.” As Frazier recalls, the influence of Motown played a significant role in shaping his style, much like hip-hop has influenced today’s NBA players. “Today you see the guys dressed like the rappers… our style was created from Motown. And I took it to another level with the Clyde. One day I bought this wide-brimmed hat and I wore it to the game and everybody go, hey, look at Clyde. And I used to steal the ball on the court.” But the nickname would eventually become much more than just a reflection of his wardrobe. “Then I was blessed enough to be the first guy to endorse a sneaker, the Puma Clyde in 1973. So that was the evolution of the mink coat, the Rolls Royce. So it was just my being around New York and observing people watching the Clyde persona personified.” On the court, Clyde helped lead the Knicks to their first two NBA championships in 1970 and 1973, with the greatest performance of his career coming in Game 7 of the 1970 NBA Finals. With the championship on the line, Frazier delivered one of the most memorable performances in NBA Finals history, scoring 36 points, dishing out a Game 7-record 19 assists, grabbing seven rebounds, and sinking all 12 of his free throws to help secure the Knicks’ first NBA title. NEW YORK, NEW YORK – MAY 04, 1970: Walt Frazier #10 of the New York Knicks drives against Jerry West #44 of the Los Angeles Lakers during Game Five of the NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden on May 04, 1970 in New York, New York. (Photo by James Drake/Getty Images) | Getty Images While Clyde’s performance in Game 7 ultimately helped lead the Knicks to their first-ever NBA championship, Clyde and his teammates also received some unexpected motivation from their captain, Willis Reed, who, despite battling a severe leg injury, famously limped onto the court just before tipoff. “People thought it was premeditated, but we did not know he was coming. So when we came on the court, we were just as flabbergasted as everybody else when we saw him.” Frazier recalls how Reed’s unexpected appearance immediately changed the team’s confidence. “By seeing him, it gave us so much confidence. And obviously, he started the game. He made his first two shots. And I thought the Lakers were psyched out from that point, and I would have the game of my life.” With two NBA championships, seven All-Star appearances, four All-NBA First Team selections, and numerous other accolades to his name, Frazier was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 1987. His No. 10 jersey also hangs in the rafters of Madison Square Garden, making him one of just eight Knicks players to have their numbers retired by the franchise. But while Frazier’s playing days eventually came to an end, his connection to the Knicks and Madison Square Garden was far from over. In 1987, Clyde began a new chapter with the organization, trading his sneakers for a microphone as he transitioned into broadcasting, where his unmistakable personality and signature style would once again make him a fixture in New York basketball. Clyde became famous for his iconic on-air rhymes, including “razzlin’ and dazzlin’” and “posting and toasting,” the latter of which inspired the name of our very own website. Frazier explained that his signature rhymes developed naturally as he gained experience in broadcasting and began to understand the nuances of being a color commentator. “The play-by-play guy does most of the talking on radio. So in order to get into sometimes what I had to say, I had to use rhymes and, you know, that’s how I started doing it.” With our website’s name paying tribute to one of Clyde’s most recognizable catchphrases, it was only fitting to ask him what he thought about Posting and Toasting. “Yeah, I read you all the time. I enjoy it, man. It’s very good.” With the Knicks winning their first championship since 1973, when Clyde hoisted his second trophy, Frazier reflected on the similarities between his championship teams and the current roster. “It’s an uncanny comparison, man. We personify a team. You can’t mention Frazier without Bradley, without Reed, without Barnett. Same thing with this team. You can’t mention Brunson without Hart, without Bridges, without KAT, without OG. So they personify a team. They’re very unselfish. They like each other. And it’s manifested in the way they play the game.” And when asked which player from the Knicks’ 2026 championship roster would have fit in best alongside his former teammates, Clyde didn’t hesitate to name the Heart of the City, Josh Hart, pointing to his versatility and physical style of play. “(Hart) rebounds, he defends, he scores, he plays with reckless abandon. So he would be that type of guy that would fit in our era, which was more physical. You know, we could hand check, push guys around the court. So I think Hart would be perfect for that era.” NEW YORK, NY – FEBRUARY 6: Josh Hart #3 and Jalen Brunson #11 of the New York Knicks congratulate Walt Frazier and Mike Breen on 25 years of broadcasting before the game against the Memphis Grizzlies on February 6, 2024 at Madison Square Garden in New York City, New York. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2024 NBAE (Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images As the 2026-27 NBA season tips off on Tuesday, October 20, with the players receiving their championship rings and the Knicks raising their third championship banner to the Madison Square Garden rafters, Clyde is teaming up with Spike Lee and AT&T for a special celebration with Knicks fans. As part of AT&T’s Connectivity Partnership, the two New York icons will travel across Manhattan in a taxi, making surprise appearances and giving fans opportunities to win exclusive NBA merchandise, signed memorabilia, and tickets to opening night. “I’m teaming up with Spike Lee, and we’re going to be going to different stores, giving out prizes for AT&T, commemorating the next championship season, and rewarding the fans as well. So I can’t believe that. It seems like we’re still in it, man. You know, everybody’s still excited about the team winning and perhaps maybe repeating, you know, running it back, which hasn’t been done in about eight years. We’ll be coming, celebrating this season throughout the season, the Knicks accomplishment. And after 53 years, the Knicks are finally back on top. Fans can walk in peace and celebrate a championship.” And while the excitement surrounding the Knicks’ championship continues into the new season, perhaps no moment captured the city’s celebration quite like the championship parade itself. As the players celebrated atop their floats and Mitchell Robinson made his way through the streets in his truck, it was only fitting that Clyde, who helped bring New York its first two championships, would lead the celebration through the Canyon of Heroes. But it wasn’t just Clyde’s presence that made the moment special. It was the car he was riding in. Frazier led the parade in the very same 1952 Chrysler Imperial Parade Phaeton that carried the Apollo 11 astronauts through the streets of Manhattan following their historic moon landing in 1969. Now that’s cool! NEW YORK, NEW YORK – JUNE 18: Walt "Clyde" Frazier celebrates during the New York Knicks Championship ticker tape parade and victory rally celebrating winning the 2026 NBA Finals on June 18, 2026 in New York City. The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs in five games to win their first NBA Championship in 53 years. (Photo by Roy Rochlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images

stories.title: Cavs rank last in local broadcast accessibility report
stories.summary: The Cavs move to streaming makes their local broadcasts more exclusive than ever before.
stories.detailText: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - JANUARY 08: A detailed view of the Cleveland Cavaliers shorts logo at Target Center on January 08, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The Timberwolves beat the Cavaliers 131-122. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Tyler Clouse/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re in a weird and fractured time for TV. Streaming services have made traditional cable packages more obsolete. This has left live sports in a weird spot, specifically in regard to local TV broadcasts. The Cleveland Cavaliers have been caught in the midst of this change. Their previous cable partner, FanDuel Sports Network, shut down at the end of last season . As a result, the Cavs and four other NBA teams turned to DAZN , a sports streaming company, to carry their local broadcasts. The Cavs announced a multi-year deal with DAZN earlier in September. It costs $119.99 to watch the Cavs’ DAZN broadcast this season. There’s also a $139.99 ultimate tier that allows for more streams and alternative angles and feeds. That dollar amount is in line with most other teams that offer a season subscription. However, the lack of over-the-air broadcasts or alternative ways to watch Cavs games locally through cable led Awful Announcing to rank the Cavs last in their local broadcast accessibility rankings . Awful Announcing’s criteria for ranking all 30 teams were simple and are explained below : “ Methodology: Each team was compared based on the cost of its direct-to-consumer streaming service, the number of major cable providers on which it is available, the number of exclusive national games, the number of over-the-air games, and the number of streaming-exclusive games ” They used that criteria to measure every team and conclude that the Cavs were the least accessible. Here’s their explanation as to why : “The Cleveland Cavaliers are the least accessible NBA team to watch for the 2026-27 season. The main reason is that they are one of five teams not available on cable, as they signed an exclusive deal with DAZN. What makes them worse than the other four teams? They will have 59 games exclusive to streaming, including DAZN, which costs $120. Then, 10 other games will be on other platforms because they are national exclusives. If the Cavaliers’ local games were on cable, that wouldn’t be such a big problem, since the package would include the national games. But because they aren’t, fans will need to subscribe to another service to watch those 10 games, in addition to the $120 they already spent on DAZN. On the bright side, at least 15 local games will be simulcast over the air.” Support us and rep the Browns with Homage! Anything bought from the links helps support Fear the Sword . You can buy the Browns throwback shirt HERE . You can also shop all of Homage’s Cleveland gear HERE . The issue with the Cavs streaming partnership is the exclusivity of the deal. If you want to watch the 59 exclusive DAZN games, you need to buy the subscription package to do so. There’s no option to bundle with cable or anything else. Additionally, it’s cheaper and easier to watch the local broadcasts of the 29 other out-of-market teams through NBA League Pass ($109.99 a season) than it is to just watch just the Cavs games in the Cleveland area. Not all teams have embraced the model that the Cavs have. The Atlanta Hawks will be broadcasting their games on Amazon Prime. While that does require a subscription (roughly $54 for the full season), that subscription comes with other perks as well, including access to other national NBA broadcasts. Other teams like the Milwaukee Bucks and Phoenix Suns are prioritizing traditional over-the-air broadcasts that just require a TV antenna to access. Both also offer streaming options as well for those who would prefer that. There’s also a conversation to be had about the increase of national NBA broadcasts. Instead of just ESPN, ABC, and TNT exclusively broadcasting national TV games, there’s now ESPN, ABC, NBC, Peacock, and Amazon Prime doing so. The latter two require subscriptions to access. Figuring out how to navigate local broadcasts in this increasingly splintered TV world is an unenviable task. It’s not as simple as it used to be when cable was much more prevalent. That said, this is an area the Cavs organization should look to improve. Being the least accessible local TV market isn’t ideal for local fans or the organization.

stories.title: Adam Silver says LeBron's helicopter deal 'perfectly appropriate' if 76ers not involved
stories.summary: The helicopter LeBron James is using to commute from New York to Philadelphia is tied to Fanatics.
stories.detailText: It's raised a few eyebrows around the league that LeBron James took a steep pay cut — playing for the veteran minimum — to come to Philadelphia, then commutes from New York to the team's New Jersey practice facility and games in Philly via helicopter. Specifically, a Fantatics-branded helicopter from the sports apparel company. Pablo Torre of the Pablo Torre Finds Out podcast — which blew the Kawhi Leonard/Clippers/Aspiration story up — said NBA owners have sent him messages asking what is going on, and he is looking into it. NBA Commissioner Adam Silver downplayed the concern in an appearance on “The Pat McAfee Show” on Tuesday, saying if it's part of LeBron's endorsement deal with Fanatics it's fine, as long as the 76ers aren't part of it ( quote via ESPN ). "He has a deal with Fanatics. It's perfectly appropriate if part of his deal is they're going to supply a helicopter to him as long as it's just a deal between the Fanatics and LeBron and no team is involved; there's no rules issue there whatsoever." Front Office Sports’ Daniel Roberts and TMZ Sports investigated LeBron's helicopter rides and endorsement deal with Fanatics, and both confirmed that LeBron isn't paying for the helicopter out of pocket. That said, LeBron has had a deal with Fanatics for several years — one that will extend beyond his playing days — and the use of the Fanatics helicopter is part of that long-term deal. Here is what a spokesperson for James told Front Office Sports : "The deal we signed with Fanatics almost three years ago includes access to their corporate aviation. It's a feature in many of their deals with their largest athletes and we appreciate their partnership as LeBron splits his time between New York and Philadelphia." Beyond that, the idea that LeBron needed a sweetener financially to take the minimum and play for Philadelphia was always a little ridiculous. Putting aside the fact that LeBron has earned more than half a billion in salary before this season ($583 million), Forbes also estimates he will make about $85 million in endorsements this year. LeBron always had the money to make the best basketball choice for himself and not stress about the payday. If the 76ers had their hands directly in LeBron's helicopter deal, that would be one thing, but it appears they don't. LeBron, for his part, recently blew all of this off, saying it was "just another way of transportation."

stories.summary: It was as if it was June again back inside Madison Square Garden as the players and their families soaked up championship ring night at the Knicks' home opener.
stories.detailText: It was as if it was June again back inside Madison Square Garden as the players and their families soaked up championship ring night at the Knicks’ home opener. The wives and girlfriends of the beloved championship team, who brought home a first NBA title to New York in 53 years, gave a behind-the-scenes look at the celebratory night Wednesday that saw two new banners go up into the rafters and 22-carat rings put on fingers . Lexi Sousa, girlfriend of Tyler Kolek, and Shannon Hart, wife of Josh Hart, both shared videos of their partners walking out to receive their rings from Walt Frazier on the court. Tyler Kolek and his girlfriend Lexi Sousa pose with his new Knicks championship ring on Wednesday night. Instagram @lexi.sousa “My champ!!” Sousa wrote over the video in an Instagram story, while Shannon inserted three smiling crying emojis in her post . Sousa also shared a photo of her and Kolek posing with the new bling following the Knicks’ 106-100 season-opening loss to the 76ers . The backup guard wore a Knicks bomber jacket with jeans and loafers while Sousa, who wore the ring, sported a shirt with No. 23 on it paired with jeans, black heels and an orange bag. Shannon Hart shares a video of her husband Josh as he walks out on the Madison Square Garden court to receive his Knicks championship ring. Instagram @shannondesiree_ “Ring szn,” she wrote . stories.title: Collin Sexton may be more important to the Lakers than expected
stories.summary: Even while not playing a single minute in the preseason, Collin Sexton showed how sorely he will be needed.
stories.detailText: If you wanted proof that absence makes the heart grow fonder, look no further than how much of a void Collin Sexton left in the Lakers’ preseason. When he signed with Los Angeles over the summer, the expectations for Sexton were simple. Get buckets, get downhill and spell Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves from having to bring the ball up the court every possession. Those duties haven’t changed. But their importance may have been undersold given the other options on the roster. With every audacious Jaden Hardy pull-up and Bronny James’ Herculean attempt to create space against an end-of-the-bench defender, it became clearer that Sexton’s skillset on the team isn’t a luxury, but rather a necessity. It is unfair and unwise to expect Sexton to replicate the caliber of offense that walked out the door with LeBron James, Marcus Smart and Luke Kennard. But he will have to be a facsimile of what they brought to the table. At 6’3”, Sexton may not look like he has the stature to take on such a large responsibility, but make no mistake, he’s a basketball-playing pitbull. He dribbles with a snarl. He dashes with a snarl. He defends with a snarl. He’s the living embodiment of a snarl. Sexton’s bite can also back up his bark. The combo guard weaves and tunnels around and underneath the defense thanks to his quick first step and plethora of inside-and-out dribbles. He attacks and asks questions second. This aggressive approach is why Sexton averaged 12.9 drives in just 23 minutes per game. For context, that number would have ranked third on the Lakers last season behind only Dončić and Reaves. It’s not just his ability to get downhill. He also has the bulk and craft to get shots up when he touches the paint. Sexton bulldozed his way to 271 attempts within five feet last season, according to the league’s tracking data . That number is more than notable players like James Harden, De’Aaron Fox and Jalen Brunson. These drives should help start the blender next to the stars and create advantages for second units devoid of shot creation. He is not the athletic runaway train that James was, but he can help ensure the north and south dimension of the offense is not absent altogether. Unlike who the Lakers trotted out in the preseason, Sexton is also simply a professional who has done the job the team requires before. With eight years of reps under his belt, Sexton has finished in the 80th percentile or higher in usage rate six times and in the 82nd percentile or higher in assist % at his position the last three seasons. Beyond his credible on-ball juice, Sexton’s outside shooting should also boost his functionality and viability in any lineup. Despite being known more for the ferocity of his drives, Sexton has quietly been one of the steadier shooting guards since entering the league. Although he is not going to shoot off pindowns or flare screens like Kennard, Sexton is not a player defenses can willfully ignore either, especially in standstill situations. Last season, Sexton converted 44.6% of his 175 catch-and-shoot threes. It’s a number that will definitely play next to two of the best drive-and-kick players in the league. Like any other role player, Sexton is also not without his warts. His aggressiveness will lead to turnovers. His defense is often more performative than impactful. And he has yet to prove himself on a team with actual postseason aspirations. All that said, the Lakers ultimately do not need Sexton to be James, Smart or even Kennard this season. That would help, but it is not realistic. Instead, they need him to be exactly who he has been throughout career with hopefully a little fine-tuning along the way. How successful he will be is still unknown as it remains to be seen when Sexton will finally make his debut . As of this piece, the guard is listed as questionable for the Lakers’ season opener against the Golden State Warriors. If the preseason was any indication, Los Angeles can not afford Sexton to miss any considerable amount of time this year. His importance is due to, yes, his underrated talent, but also the uninspiring caliber of the Lakers’ alternatives. For the team’s sake, Sexton’s value this season will be derived from the former. stories.title: How the Pistons’ pulled off the NBA’s biggest opening day comeback ever
stories.summary: The NBA is back, and there's nothing like a sunny fall afternoon in the gym
stories.detailText: (Photo by Chris Schwegler/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images DETROIT — Jalen Duren looked like a heavyweight boxer who had just gone three rounds 45 minutes before the Detroit Pistons faced the Boston Celtics for the NBA’s 2026-27 season opener on Tuesday afternoon. Duren, wearing white cutoffs and black Pistons sweatpants, was already dripping with perspiration as he put in extra work on his driving and pull-up mid-range shooting with an assistant coach prior to tip-off. The rare 3 p.m. local start time didn’t take away any of the intensity from a meeting between two of the best teams in the Eastern Conference, and it was clear even before jump ball that neither side would be easing into the new season. It felt like the Celtics landed a knockout punch midway through the third quarter when Paul George ripped the nets for another three-pointer to put Boston up 22 points. The Pistons appeared to have the same structural problems that tanked a 60-win team in the playoffs last season: not enough shooting or creation next to star Cade Cunningham, and too many lineups that lacked two-way balance. That’s when Detroit subbed Javonte Green into the game for the first time, and immediately flipped the switch. The Pistons beat the Celtics, 121-113, for the biggest opening night comeback in league history. Detroit was fueled by a 23-0 fourth quarter run where its defense held the Celtics scoreless for five minutes in crunch time. “I think the comeback just embodied the culture and what we’re trying to build here,” Duren said after the win. “We’re a team that’s known to be gritty, known to get it out the mud, known to never quit.” Pistons INSANE 23-0 run vs Celtics. pic.twitter.com/piJbJL5rz3 — Basketball Performances (@NBAPerformances) October 20, 2026 Duren needed to get off to a good start after missing the first week of training camp with a lingering contract dispute that caused hurt feelings on both sides. That storyline can be put to rest now after he finished with 22 points and nine rebounds on 8-of-13 shooting, an excellent performance that almost felt quiet in real time because of how he accumulated his numbers. Everything was in the flow of the offense on lobs, putbacks, and dunker’s spot finishes, and his best work might not have even showed up in the box score. The Celtics optimize every aspect of the game under Joe Mazzulla, with shot location and generating extra possessions being paramount to their success. Boston crashes the offensive glass as hard as any team in the league, and it added perhaps the single greatest offensive rebounder alive this side of Houston’s Steven Adams by inking Mitchell Robinson to a three-year deal over the summer. Well, Robinson was mostly invisible in this game, with Duren and his teammates boxing out hard on every possession. Yes, Robinson did turn an ankle in the first half before returning, but that’s both part of the game and a major part of the deal with Robinson in particular. The Pistons out-rebounded the Celtics with a 49-39 edge on the glass. “It’s not only their bigs, but their smaller players, too. They’re known to crash from the corners. My mindset tonight was whether I get the rebound or not, I just got to keep them off the glass,” Duren told me after the game . This will be remembered as the Javonte Green game for good reason. Green didn’t play in the first half, but head coach JB Bickerstaff knew he needed a spark in the third quarter as the Celtics were turning it into a rout. Part of Boston’s game-plan is ignoring non-shooters on the perimeter, but they didn’t get the memo that Green has turned himself into a viable outside threat in recent years. Green knocked down 5-of-8 threes, most of them wide open, to give Detroit new life. His defense was just as important by getting into the gaps and helping make Jayson Tatum settle for tough jumpers that he was consistently bricking. Tatum finished 6-of-23 from the floor. Green ended the night +21 in 18 minutes. The Pistons looked far more formidable in his minutes than they did with John Collins or Ron Holland on the floor, and it makes sense. Green doesn’t hesitate to shoot from three on offense, he has active hands and tons of bounce on the defensive end, and he consistently plays a team game by moving the ball to the open man. He’s everything you want out of a role player, and he’s one of the few Detroit reserves who actually offers a two-way game when his shot is falling like it did Tuesday. Duncan Robinson was also excellent. He knocked down 5-of-9 threes by sprinting around screens and firing with just a sliver of space. When he didn’t have a clean look, Robinson would hit the brakes, go into his shot, and get fouled by Celtics defenders who were rushing to close out on him. With Robinson, Isaiah Joe, and Kevin Huerter, the Pistons actually have some options to improve their spacing around Cunningham this season, though building lineups that can actually compete defensively with viable three-point shooting will continue to be Bickerstaff’s biggest challenge. The Pistons won 14 games three seasons ago. They made a massive jump to 44 wins two years ago, and another big leap to 60 wins and the No. 1 seed in the East last season. Detroit doesn’t really have much room to improve in the regular season, but there’s still tons of upside left in their playoff approach. The Pistons would have been the victims of a 1-8 first-round upset if Franz Wagner didn’t get hurt for the Magic. Duren was out-played by an inferior player in Wendell Carter Jr. in the series, and he didn’t look much better in round two as Detroit was eliminated by an uninspiring Cavs team. “We’ve seen the bottom, so we’re not afraid of it,” Duren said of his team’s slow start through the first three quarters. “I’d never say we were scared or worried. We knew we had to pick it up, and we did.” It’s not obvious where the Pistons’ next step is coming from yet, but that’s okay. It’s a long season, and Detroit will discover plenty of things along the way, just like they did on opening night with Green’s unexpected explosion. The East is better than ever , but the Pistons aren’t going to be scared of anyone. The Knicks’ opening night loss to the Philadelphia 76ers in the very next game only reinforced the idea that the conference is wide open. New York deserves to be the favorite as the defending champs, but there’s about seven other East teams that can realistically dream of making an NBA Finals run, and Detroit is one of them. The early tip-off time didn’t feel like a nuisance in and around the arena. Before the game, fans decked out in Celtics and Pistons gear embraced each other outside to welcome back NBA basketball. It was nice to see a mutual respect from both sides at the start of a long season. When the top-8 of the East is as bunched up as it appears to be entering the new year, every game matters, and for one afternoon the Pistons got the better of the Celtics. While it’s just one night, this game did give both teams plenty to chew on. The Celtics were “guarding” Ausar Thompson with a big man who roamed off him 15-feet away from the perimeter, daring him to shoot. Thompson still found a way to make an offensive impact even with arguably the league’s ugliest jump shot by cutting to the rim, spraying out quick passes for three-point attempts, and getting out in the open floor. His 360 scoop layup in the first half was a thing of beauty. He finished the game +12 in his 33 minutes, and harassed Tatum with his all-world perimeter defense. Other teams will have to wonder if playing off him to that degree is really worth it. 360 SPINNING LAYUP. Sweet move by Ausar Thompson on NBC and Peacock 😳 pic.twitter.com/e46aKoXRZu — NBA (@NBA) October 20, 2026 George looked unreal in his Celtics debut after coming over in the controversial Jaylen Brown trade . He finished with 38 points, five rebounds, and five steals on 7-of-12 shooting from three. He’s going to be a natural fit in the Celtics’ system if he can stay healthy. Tatum looked great in the first half and terrible in the second. I thought Boston needed more Payton Pritchard to loosen things up offensively. Why is Joe Mazzulla bringing him off the bench? Hugo Gonzalez, the king of Time Decay RAPM, was dreadful in his 10 minutes, finishing -15. I thought Baylor Scheierman looked great, and the Neemias Queta minutes were more promising than Robinson’s. An 82-game regular season is just too damn long, but there’s nothing like NBA games that actually feel meaningful. Duren called it a playoff atmosphere after the game, and it really did seem like it. I was exhausted just watching his pre-game workout before he went out and dunked everything at the basket while winning the battle on the boards that truly dictates wins and losses. Overreact to this game if you want to. I’m not going to judge you. For one sunny fall afternoon in the Midwest, it just felt so nice to be back in the gym.
