stories.title: Will Kawhi Leonard have his jersey retired? Toronto embraces the most unique legacy in the NBA
stories.summary: As Leonard kicks off his second tenure with Toronto, do the Raptors represent his best shot at having his jersey retired?
stories.detailText: As we tip off the 2026-27 season, I don't begrudge NBA fans who are desperately trying to make sense of this past offseason. We are right there with you. LeBron James and Jaylen Brown are Sixers? Giannis Antetokounmpo is in South Beach? The Washington Wizards gave Trae Young how much ? The biggest plot twist, however, involves our friends north of the border. In the aftermath of the stiffest punishment in NBA history handed down by commissioner Adam Silver on LA Clippers owner Steve Ballmer and his eternally beleaguered franchise, Kawhi Leonard has largely escaped unscathed. And not only that, Leonard, the grand prize of the Clippers' cap circumvention, has returned to the team that originally flagged cap circumvention shadiness to the league office when he left — the Toronto Raptors. Yes, Kawhi Leonard is a Raptor, picking up where he left off in 2019 in a quest to bring another title to Canada. He continues what is the most confusing NBA legacy of his generation. A two-time Finals MVP, seven-time All-NBA selection and two-time Defensive Player of the Year who, as of now, is no lock to have his jersey retired by any of his former teams. It's a question that I can't stop thinking about as NBA fans wrestle with how one of the game's greats will be remembered following a historic cap scandal: Do the Raptors represent Leonard's best shot at having his jersey retired? In the player empowerment era, the fascinating case of Leonard could help shape the legacies of his superstar peers who jump from team to team. Kawhi Leonard kicks off his second tenure with Toronto. (AP Photo/Frank Franklin II) AP Photo/Frank Franklin II Leonard's legacy? Imagine telling an NBA fan in 2017 how this Kawhi Leonard story would play out. At the time, Leonard had earned back-to-back Defensive Player of the Year awards, had already won a championship and a Finals MVP. The Spurs were coming off back-to-back 60-win seasons, and Leonard was the face of it all. If you look up in the rafters at the Spurs' arena, you'll see Timmy, Tony and Manu's jerseys up there. And for a while, it seemed like Leonard's No. 2 jersey would be right next to them. But things in San Antonio soured quickly. After some disagreements about how the team handled his knee injury, Kawhi's magical rise with the Spurs had a sudden and bitter downfall. Leonard played just nine games in the 2017-18 season and, in the summer of 2018, the Spurs traded Kawhi and Danny Green to the Raptors for DeMar DeRozan, Jakob Poeltl and a top-20 protected 2019 first-round draft pick. Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season Spurs fans weren't happy with how it all went down. Every time Leonard played in San Antonio, boos rained down from every corner of the arena. But Gregg Popovich, Leonard's longtime coach, was not pleased with it. In a November matchup in 2023 against Leonard's Clippers, Popovich took the PA announcer's microphone in the middle of Leonard's trip to the free-throw line and demanded an end to the booing. "Excuse me for a second," Popovich said. "Can we stop all the booing and let these guys play? Have a little class. That's not who we are. Knock off the booing." Coach Pop's backing was unusual, but it did reveal a continued heartfelt connection with his former Finals MVP who left on uneasy terms. Leonard's reception in San Antonio may still be icy, but if history is a guide, the team will honor him one day with a jersey retirement. And so will the Raptors. Even if he played just one season in Toronto. The case to retire Kawhi's jersey In January, the Raptors will hold a ceremony to retire Kyle Lowry's No. 7 jersey alongside Vince Carter's No. 15 in the Toronto rafters. Lowry's case is a no-brainer. He appeared in 409 Raptors wins, making him the winningest player in franchise history. He is also the franchise leader in assists, steals, made 3s, triple-doubles and All-Star appearances. And for that, just a few weeks ago, the Raptors unveiled their Kyle Lowry statue, which is comically not Lowry at all, but a dinosaur with a basketball jersey on. Though it may seem controversial now, it seems likely that Kawhi Leonard's No. 2 jersey will join No. 7 and No. 15 one day. Based on one standard, there's no question that Leonard will have his jersey retired by the Raptors. I researched every Finals MVP winner in NBA history and looked to see if the franchise had retired his jersey. And here are the facts: There have been 28 Finals MVPs who are no longer playing in the NBA. All 28 of them have seen their jerseys rise up to the rafters of their respective buildings. That list of Finals MVPs includes Cedric Maxwell of the Boston Celtics and Andre Iguodala of the Golden State Warriors. They are the only Finals MVPs who have had their jersey retired but have not been inducted into the Hall of Fame. And they help set a precedent for Leonard, who won Finals MVP in both San Antonio and Toronto. But here's the thing: Maxwell and Iguodala each logged eight seasons with their Finals MVP teams. If it weren't for this trade back to Toronto, Leonard would be the shortest-tenured Finals MVP in league history. A one-and-done mercenary of this magnitude had never been seen before. Besides Kawhi, no player had ever left his team immediately after winning the Finals MVP. (That is, if you exclude Michael Jordan's two retirements with the Bulls.) According to my research — which, I should note, excludes memorial jersey retirements like Reggie Lewis in Boston and Bobby Phills in Charlotte — Leonard would become one of four honored players who played fewer than four seasons with a team. Another caveat, this list does not count those who were players and coaches for their club, like Lenny Wilkens and Nate McMillan in Seattle, who muddy up the picture. SHORTEST NUMBER OF SEASONS FOR RETIRED JERSEY Player Franchise Tenure (Yrs) Michael Jordan MIA 0 Kawhi Leonard* TOR 1 Nate Thurmond CLE 2 Julius Erving BKN 3 Jordan had his No. 23 retired by the Miami Heat in 2003 when legendary coach and exec Pat Riley decided to pay tribute to MJ. It is the one instance of an NBA team retiring a jersey of a player who's played less than a season with their club. (Did you ever wonder why LeBron James wore No. 6 and not No. 23 in Miami?) Nate Thurmond had his No. 42 jersey retired by the Cleveland Cavaliers despite playing in just one and a half seasons with the team and averaging a measly five points per game as the backup center. Look up "The Miracle of Richfield" sometime and you'll begin to understand Thurmond's legacy in Northeast Ohio. Not to mention the future Hall of Famer was from Akron, Ohio. Kawhi is under contract for three more seasons, thanks to a contract extension signed this offseason. He can opt out after two seasons, which would bring his total seasons in Toronto to three. Even if Kawhi plays just three seasons in Toronto, it wouldn't be the shortest tenure. Julius Erving had his jersey retired by the 76ers, but also by the Nets. In just three seasons with New York, Dr. J led the Nets to two championships and won three MVPs in the ABA. Let's say Kawhi picks up his player option for the 2028-29 and finishes out his career with the Raptors after four seasons. How exclusive is the Four Seasons club? There are nine players who have had their jerseys retired with just four seasons in uniform. Shaq has done it twice. The underlying throughline for most of these guys is relevant to Kawhi — seven of the 10 instances were driven by a championship run. JERSEY RETIRED WITH JUST 4 SEASONS Player Franchise Tenure (Yrs) Titles Clyde Drexler HOU 4 1 Shaquille O'Neal MIA 4 1 Oscar Robertson MIL 4 1 Wilt Chamberlain PHI 4 1 Bill Walton POR 4 1 Dave Twardzik POR 4 1 Lionel Hollins POR 4 1 Pete Maravich ATL 4 0 Charles Barkley PHX 4 0 Shaquille O'Neal ORL 4 0 Given that every retired Finals MVP has had his jersey honored by his team and the fact that there have been several instances of retired jerseys for players with short tenures with their clubs, Kawhi can expect to see No. 2 join No. 7 and No. 15 one day in Toronto. NBA superstars will be watching how the Raptors handle Leonard's situation. What about other NBA superstars? In the player empowerment era headlined by LeBron James, it's common for the modern NBA superstar to switch teams in his prime, leaving various franchises with some tough decisions about jersey immortality. Kevin Durant, for example, will have a fascinating case ahead of him. Will the No. 35 be retired in OKC? One hint is that, a year after KD left, PJ Dozier was allowed to wear No. 35 for OKC in 2017-18. "Honestly I didn't even think twice about [Durant having it] ... I just saw it was open and took advantage of it." The Thunder could still decide to honor Durant one day, and I suspect they will. His jersey could be retired by the Golden State Warriors as well, even though he played only three seasons there. He won two titles (and two Finals MVPs) in the Bay like Dr. J in New York. Elsewhere, Brooklyn, Phoenix and Houston would have less pressure to do so, considering he didn't reach past the second round in any of those three stops. Yet. In the non-Finals-MVP department, Anthony Davis should also be curious about Kawhi. Davis left New Orleans on icy terms and, like Kawhi, won a title in his first season with his new club, the Lakers. Davis played longer in LA than Kawhi did in Toronto, but the Lakers may be a little pickier considering they have so many numbers retired as is. Jimmy Butler is another superstar with a chance of retiring without being honored by a team. The six-time All-Star and five-time All-NBA standout has made a lasting impact in Chicago and Miami, but enough to be honored with a jersey retirement? Chris Paul has strong cases in New Orleans and Los Angeles, but the latter franchise has seemingly sent the wrong messages. The Clippers already gave Paul's No. 3 to Bradley Beal this summer, months after they waived Paul unceremoniously in the middle of his farewell tour. It seems ludicrous that LA wouldn't honor Lob City with jersey retirements for Paul, Blake Griffin and DeAndre Jordan. But according to Griffin , he isn't exactly holding his breath on having his jersey retired by the Clippers. But the guy who might be watching Kawhi's legacy closest? How about Paul George? When they joined forces in 2019, it marked the biggest free-agency coup in franchise history and both seemed destined to be honored by the Clippers one day. Now, after the Kawhi scandal has tarnished his tenure with the team and considering George's association with that era, it's not looking too good that either of them will have their jerseys retired in the Intuit Dome. Which leads us to this unbelievable fact. The Clippers are the only NBA team to not have any retired numbers in their 57-year history. Not from their San Diego days or the Buffalo Braves days. Zero jerseys hang in the Intuit rafters. Every retired Finals MVP has had his jersey raised to the rafters by his respective team, but not every MVP, as it turns out. The Clippers, who came from San Diego after the Buffalo Braves relocated, have not retired Bob McAdoo's jersey despite him winning the MVP award in 1975 with the Braves. It's a shame the Clippers should correct soon. That's maybe the most twisted thing about this entire Kawhi Leonard jersey retirement story. He was the Clippers' best chance at having their first jersey up in the rafters. But now? Good luck getting that past Adam Silver. The Clippers keep circumventing their own chances at having a jersey retirement ceremony one day. But as Leonard kicks off his second tenure with Toronto, he's all but certain to have his jersey retired by the Raptors. A second championship would remove all doubt.

stories.title: Failure to rebound spells Celtics’ doom in season opener vs. Pistons
stories.summary: The Pistons outrebounded the Celtics 49 to 39, winning them the possession game
stories.detailText: DETROIT, MI - OCTOBER 20: Jalen Duren #0 of the Detroit Pistons and Neemias Queta #88 of the Boston Celtics looks on during the game on October 20, 2026 at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit, Michigan. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Chris Schwegler/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Boston Celtics’ season opener against the Detroit Pistons started with nerves and excitement followed by confidence and joy, but ultimately resulted in sheer disappointment . The Celtics blew a 22-point second-half lead, falling 121-113. It was just one game out of 82 and after Boston’s longest offseason in 10 years, you take it with a grain of salt. But before moving on, it’s important to learn from it to avoid repeating future mistakes, though. Outside of the poor shooting numbers from Tatum and the stagnating offense in the second half, the most glaring mistake was letting Detroit beat them on the boards. The Pistons outrebounded the Celtics 49 to 39 over the course of the game. They won on both the offensive and defensive glass, 14 to 12, and 35 to 27, respectively. With the possession battle being such a crucial part of Joe Mazzulla’s philosophy, I would have expected a different outcome. Last season, Mitchell Robinson and Neemias Queta were both in the top-20 best rebounders across the league. Mitch (13 th ) averaged 8.8 rebounds per game, while Neemi averaged 8.4. In the opener, they combined for just 7 total rebounds, 3 from Robinson, 4 from Queta. Boston’s effort on the glass was led by Jordan Walsh at 6, followed by Paul George with 5, by far their two most active players all night. On the other side, Jalen Duren picked up 9 rebounds, John Collins had 5, and Paul Reed added in another 6. Though not a big, Ausar Thompson led all players with 11 boards. Sometimes the ball just doesn’t bounce your way, but it felt like Detroit consistently had better activity and positioning. They rallied to the paint as a team, usually sending at least two or three bodies to box out or gather up longer rebounds. It’s a big reason they were able to effectively neutralize Queta and Robinson in the matchup. Oct 20, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Boston Celtics center Neemias Queta (88) and Detroit Pistons guard Javonte Green (31) go for the rebound in the second half at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Mitchell Robinson wasn’t very happy with his performance. He tweaked his ankle early in the game, but it didn’t end his night as he decided to play through it. When asked about it after the game, he didn’t use it as an excuse, instead shouldering the blame. “I got my a** kicked on the glass,” he said. “I can’t have no starts like that. It’s cool to get out there and put on that Boston jersey for the first time in a regular-season game, but overall, I still didn’t do what I needed to do. I gotta compete better. I feel like I didn’t compete at a high level that I normally do and I was kind of slow on a lot of things.” Boston still had to work for their boards; very few were uncontested. That’s likely going to be the case most nights, which only means they have to work harder. The three-pointers will be the headline, but Detroit’s energy is what caused the game to flip. They limited the Celtics to single possessions, fueling their long, unanswered runs. They also picked up 24 second chance points compared to Boston’s 16, which helped them overcome their slight disadvantage in the shooting splits. It perfectly encapsulates exactly why Mazzulla emphasizes the possession game. More possessions amount to more opportunities, meaning that you are more tolerant to faults. I’m sure we’ll see plenty more nights where the offense stagnates and shots don’t fall. The best way to combat that is to crash the offensive glass and try to generate better looks when the defense doesn’t have a chance to set, or is scrambling to do so. On the other end, limiting opponents to one possession also ensures that you don’t fall in too deep of a hole, or in this case, don’t let them dig themselves out of the one you put them in. Again, this is only game one of 82. The Celtics have plenty of time to correct themselves. Thanks to the early start, they have two and a half nights to review film before their first home game of the season, a matchup with the rival New York Knicks. Mitchell Robinson and crew will have a chance to redeem themselves while going up against his former teammates, including last year’s rebound leader, Karl Anthony-Towns.

stories.title: How will the Rockets do this season?
stories.summary: Time for another fun season.
stories.detailText: Happy start of the NBA Season! With the Rockets’ season kicking off at home against the Dallas Mavericks, I figured now was a good time to get into my pre-season predictions. Just a note before we start: all odds come from FanDuel, which you can view here . Additonally, if you want a more in depth breakdown of any certain player you can check out our season preview series here . How many games will Houston win, and what seed will they be? To start, I predict Houston will record 55 wins. This would be three more wins than last season and would likely leave Houston as a top-three or top-four seed. For context, FanDuel has Houston at +1000 for seventh seed, +2000 for first seed, +850 for second seed seed, +1300 for eighth seed, +470 for fourth seed, +450 for third seed, and +320 for 55+ wins. Who will be the top scorer? For my top scorer I have Alperen Sengun, however I would not be surprised if Amen Thompson was the leading scorer, and I would be content as long as Kevin Durant is not the leading scorer BECAUSE WHY ARE WE PLACING THAT MUCH OF A BURDEN ON 38-YEAR-OLD KEVIN DURANT? Breakout young player? I was between Jabari Smith jr. and Reed Sheppard for breakout player, but for me once a player has seccured their second NBA contract, they are now longer qualified for breakout young player. I think Reed Sheppard will defenitley have a smaller role at times this season because of the return of Fred Vanvleet, and the additon of Marcus Smart, however, I think a smaller role may be better for him, as it will give him less pressure. Instead of being thrust into the rotation as the backup point guard after playing very few NBA rotation minutes the prior year, Reed will get consistent spot minutes allowing him to serve as an off the bench sniper. Think Gerald Green’s role of a off the bench siniper, but as a better player. Leading bench contributor? Now for this category, it depends on what you count as a contributor. Are you going off scoring numbers and stats, or overall impact? Depending on your answer, I have two different options for leading bench contributor: one being Marcus Smart, and the other being Tari Eason. To start off with Smart, having someone besides Fred VanVleet who can run the offense will be nothing short of exceptional, but that’s not even where Smart fully shines. Houston is potentially adding another top NBA defender to its roster that already includes Amen Thompson, Tari Eason, and Jabari Smith Jr., along with other good defenders. Now imagine if Marcus gets his three pointer back to leauge average, or even above league average, and we are COOKING. Now the case for Tari over Marcus is that Tari is likely, in my opinion, to have higher counting stats, and the possibility that Marcus may end up starting if Fred misses time or sits out back-to-backs, but I think you can really have either Tari or Smart penciled in for the largest bench contributor. I did also consider Bogdan Bogdanovic, but I feel he is more of a cleanup crew end of the bench kinda guy who will see spot minutes on occasion. How far will Houston go? Now for the million-dollar question: do I expect Houston to win a championship this year? Unfortunately, as much as I would like to say they could win, I can’t say that in good conscience, as San Antonio and Oklahoma City appear to be in a tier of their own. Now could Houston win a title? Sure, but I could also wake up one day with an extra toe. I think my prediction is a second- or third-round exit, and I can see either one happening. It likely will depend on if they can avoid the Spurs/Thunder till the WCF. Now with all that out of the way, I want to know YOUR season predictions for the Rockets season. Who do you expect to be the leading scorer? How many games do you have Houston winning? Let us know in the comments, and as always, make sure to check back at The Dream Shake for all things Houston Rockets news, analysis, and more.

teamStories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO, TX - OCTOBER 20: Victor Wembanyama #1 of the San Antonio Spurs & Chet Holmgren #7 of the Oklahoma City Thunder battle for the opening top off on October 20, 2026 at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photos by Michael Gonzales/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images I don’t think I was ready for the season to start. After that car crash of a series in June where we watched the Spurs’ magical run go up in flames, I just shut everything down. I simply did my best not to think about it. I tried watching baseball. I tried going outside. It’s not “repressing your feelings” if you’re doing it in a healthy way, right? And it worked. Mostly. I spent the whole summer without rage baiting myself with clips of the OG’s tip-in or Knicks fans dancing around in our building. I didn’t watch the draft. I didn’t follow the offseason. I boycotted the most controversial SNL host of the year (Jalen Brunson). You know, it’s often said that cool guys don’t look back at explosions, but sad boys don’t look at them either. The flames are hot but the heart is chill . I was feeling pretty good about everything, in the sense that I was feeling nothing at all. The only real downside to this strategy was realizing I maybe took the bit a little too far when Opening Night sort of materialized out of nowhere. Tuesday night? This Tuesday? No. Really? If the Spurs were playing on Tuesday I would’ve heard about it. In spite of all my best efforts to ignore the dripping faucet noises coming from down the hall, the reality of my flooded emotional basement was aggressively brought to my attention come tip-off against the Thunder last night. The peaceful calm I had worked all summer to cultivate dissipated in moments. Hartenstein hit a layup. Shai hit a three. We were already down two points and I wanted to die. The season was 3 minutes old and I was as miserable now as I was watching another 4th quarter lead against the Knicks disappear in June. Crap. For the first time in my living memory, it was not fun to have the Spurs back in my life. I wasn’t awash in the glow of anticipation that a new season usually brings. Where I normally would be drooling about the prospects of what could go right, I was instead drowning in the possibilities of what could go wrong. Do I think my bad attitude somehow bled across time and space, infecting the Spurs with terrible energy and leading to a truly putrid first half? No. No? Yeah, No. However! Did what I watched eerily reflect the deep, black rot I could feel manifesting itself in my basketball soul? Suspiciously so. Mitch Johnson said afterward that they came out too amped and put their energy in all the wrong places. Stephon Castle said they were taking the first good shot instead of making Oklahoma City work for it. I know that feeling. It’s what happens when you spend months pretending you can’t see the monster in the corner, and then when something else walks into the room you just start swinging at whatever. What I’m using entirely too many words and overwrought metaphors to say is…the vibes just feel off. At media day, everything the Spurs said sounded like a team facing it head-on. Wemby said they weren’t going to hide from any of it. Motivation, accountability. I’d love to imagine that’s all it takes to shake off last June, reload, and go again. It sounded right. But the Knicks series was a Ray Allen level emotional event, and whatever they did this summer, they didn’t show up Tuesday looking like a team that had made peace with anything. It doesn’t feel fine. In the second quarter, we were down nine, and De’Aaron Fox threw Chet Holmgren to the floor. Like, full on, WWE tossed him to the ground. I grimly nodded along. The game was slipping, the shots weren’t falling, and some feral part of me stopped wanting to watch basketball and started wanting to watch a fight. Forget the basketball, let’s just go at it, and whoever is left standing can continue on to play Houston on Friday. It was, frankly, the only moment all night I couldn’t look away from. Over the next six and a half minutes, they outscored us 22-5. By the time the dust settled it was 59-33. Maybe I’m wrong. I’ve been guilty of projecting all of my own weird stuff onto a group of guys that are just trying to go out and play some basketball before, and I can assure you I’ll be guilty of it again. But this team seems to me like it has a wound. A deep wound that hasn’t healed yet, and I’m not exactly sure how that’s going to look as the season wears on. This team isn’t like the 2014 squad, a crew of battle-tested vets who had been through the ringer and knew how to claw their way back. This is everyone’s first time dealing with the pain and heartbreak that comes with coming so close to the ultimate prize, only to have their dreams detonated on the biggest stage imaginable. Mitch Johnson isn’t Gregg Popovich. Yet. Castle and Harper aren’t Tony and Manu. Yet. Victor Wembanyama isn’t Tim Duncan. Yet. There’s no real roadmap for how to fix this. It’s going to be a process and it might look pretty messy for a while. It’s the type of thing that might linger a lot longer than any of us are comfortable with. Brace yourselves. Time will tell if this group can do that work on the fly, but if we learned anything last night, it’s that whatever broke last June isn’t fixed and everything else is on hold until it is. Takeaways I feel very wrong-footed by the idea that Victor is just sort of reviled on the national stage now. One minute everyone was on board with us overthrowing the Thunder and then, all of a sudden, it’s sort of just become accepted that he is a villain in the league. It’s been agreed that he’s just embraced this heel turn or whatever and we’re all just kind of along for that ride. I don’t love it. In fact, I kind of hate it? I know there are reasons. People think he’s arrogant (he is) and people think he’s French (he is) and people think he elbowed Naz Reid in the head (allegedly). Whatever. Look, nothing matters beyond what we think about him and we think he rules so I guess we’re just rallying around the flag. Seems unfair though! That said, Wemby, need you to hit a few more shots, brother. One silver lining to the fiasco that was opening night is that the game doesn’t actually count because Tobias Harris wasn’t playing. Enjoy the big fat asterisk on your good vibes, OKC. Toby’s coming for you! I know it’s just one game, but melting into my seat as three after three got flung up at the basket only to jarringly clang off the rim was dispiriting. The Spurs went 10-for-37 from deep, and Castle accounted for half of those. I don’t think I can live like that all year. I like the three-guard lineup, and Tuesday is the best evidence I have. Fox, Castle and Harper started the second half together and the Spurs went on a 23-9 run to chop a 21-point deficit down to seven. Those three scored all 23 points, 11 of them from Castle, while Wemby didn’t score at all. Mitch Johnson had them split up for most of the first half, and I think they only got only like 12ish minutes together all night. I’m glad we’re leaning into it. Let’s lean more! Let’s go! WWL Post Game Press Conference Another season on deck, are you ready? Not even remotely. I’m woefully unprepared. Didn’t you hear me up there? I was watching baseball all summer. I was going on hikes. I don’t even remember how this was sport is supposed to work. I couldn’t remember my Peacock login. I’m a mess. It’s all a mess. Oh no! Yea it’s bad. I truly just like, I mean it’s been a long time since the Spurs went that far in the playoffs, I think I just wasn’t ready for the summer to feel so short. I’m lashing out because I feel cheated out of time to like regroup and reconnect with my feelings. I mean, you did have almost four months to do that. Yea but, like I said I was watching baseball. Who’s going to win the World Series? The fans. Lame .

teamStories.detailText: Consider Oct. 21, 2025: NBA opening night inside Crypto.com Arena. A 40-year-old LeBron James , who hadn't missed a season opener in his 23-year career, is watching from the bench with a nagging sciatica that would push his season debut -- in his final year under contract with the Los Angeles Lakers -- to mid-November. Which of the following would've been the most surprising if you had a crystal ball (and chose NBA opening night 2026) to see into the future: James, now 41, still playing at a high level, for the Philadelphia 76ers , at ... center? James' distaste for playing defensive center spans decades because of the wear and tear. But his move there at times Tuesday night, albeit alongside big man Joel Embiid for much of it, should be one of the biggest takeaways from the 76ers' 106-100 win at Madison Square Garden. Not only did he play backup center at times Tuesday night, but there were numerous possessions where James defended Knicks center Karl-Anthony Towns , with Embiid sliding to guard Josh Hart . It enabled the 76ers to better defend Towns in the pick-and-roll. James also made plays as a basket defender, including during his pivotal late-game block on Mikal Bridges . Common sense dictates that James won't play 34 minutes as he did Tuesday -- nor play this much center -- over the long haul of the season. But Game 1 revealed both the role James is willing to play for Philadelphia and a willingness from coach Nick Nurse to get creative right away. More takeaways from opening night Point KAT largely absent from Knicks offense Jalen Brunson shot 6-for-19. Bridges shot 2-for-8. OG Anunoby was 1-from-9 from behind the arc, where New York shot a meager 37% as a team. Towns had one assist. When the Knicks swept (a very different) 76ers team in the 2026 playoffs, Towns averaged 7.5 assists per game, as New York's title run relied heavily on his ability as a trigger man at the top of the offense. That was missing from Tuesday's game plan. Early foul trouble played a role, but there is a track record that the more touches Towns gets, the more potent the Knicks' offense can be. The ball wasn't sticking in Philly's new offense Other than Tyrese Maxey , who had 28 points, none of the Sixers had a great offensive night; James and Embiid combined to shoot 9-for-28. But the stars followed through with a principle Nurse has instilled since training camp: encourage ball movement. And that was absolutely working. Embiid and James combined for 13 assists, while Maxey and Jaylen Brown combined for 11. This is a cornerstone of how the 76ers want and need to play. They have a lot of offensive talent -- Anfernee Simons ' 13 points off the bench is part of that -- but to use it they have to share the ball. This, in theory, should make Philadelphia a resilient team this season. It did on opening night. Rookie Aday Mara instantly impacts the Wemby battle Over the past year, Victor Wembanyama has given Oklahoma City nightmares game-planning for the team's biggest obstacle to the Finals. There is no easy solution; in fact, there might ultimately not be a solution at all. But one of the measures the Thunder took was to draft Mara with the No. 12 pick in June, which they got from the LA Clippers as part of the Kawhi Leonard trade in 2019. Within minutes of Mara being selected on draft night, he was talking about how he knew he was going to be needed for the Spurs matchups. Mara didn't dominate summer league, but he got in better shape as the offseason progressed. He had an excellent preseason and was effective right away as the first big off the bench. Just as they did last season, the Thunder used Isaiah Hartenstein , Chet Holmgren and Alex Caruso on Wembanyama. But adding Mara to the committee gives them another option in this fight. Detroit's defense already looks familiar The Pistons won their opening matchup with the Celtics with offense, particularly the 10 combined 3-pointers by Duncan Robinson and Javonte Green as they scored a whopping 78 points in the second half. But the Pistons' defense remained the same level of last season's 60-win team despite some personnel changes, namely replacing Tobias Harris and Isaiah Stewart . The Pistons, led by Jalen Duren and Ausar Thompson , were stout on the interior as they held the Celtics to just 34 paint points. And Detroit limited centers Mitchell Robinson and Neemias Queta to just two offensive rebounds, with Duren and Thompson combining for 14 defensive rebounds.

teamStories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO -- It took every bit of three quarters to do it, but Victor Wembanyama scrapped to earn his first bucket in Tuesday's 116-104 loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder . Unfortunately for the San Antonio Spurs , it didn't come until the buzzer sounded to end the third quarter. Wembanyama fought through Chet Holmgren crossing half court, then set a screen on Cason Wallace before rolling to the basket for a spinning dunk off a lob from De'Aaron Fox . He missed his previous 12 shots up to that point, tying the mark for the second-most missed field goals to start a season opener in the play-by-play era (since 1997-98), according to Elias. Wembanyama would finish the night shooting a career-worst 8% (1-for-13) from the field with 12 points, 13 rebounds and six blocks. "I need to go back to playing the basketball I like," Wembanyama said. "This is not the sport I like right here. I've got no reason to be hesitant, no reason to not be myself. I'm good when I have fun. I missed a lot of shots I usually don't miss. But after that, I didn't go back to these shots, and I wasn't decisive. I might be overthinking it. I don't need to do more. I need to think less probably." Wembanyama shot 52.4% from the field last season in five regular-season games against Oklahoma City, averaging 18.4 points, as the Spurs rolled to a 4-1 record against the Thunder. In the Western Conference finals, Wembanyama boosted his scoring average against OKC to 27.3 points on 48.1% shooting from the floor. Yet finding offensive success against the Thunder in Tuesday's opener proved much more difficult. Oklahoma City constantly showed the 22-year-old crowds while providing an optimal blend of help defense without letting San Antonio's other scorers loose. Holmgren made up for a rough showing against Wembanyama in the Western Conference finals with an assertive, physical performance against him Tuesday and contributed 14 points and seven rebounds. Holmgren swatted away a Wembanyama runner in the second quarter for one of his team-high four blocks. Rookie big man Aday Mara also logged a block against Wembanyama on a potential dunk off a Fox alley-oop. Isaiah Hartenstein chipped in, too. "I thought he missed shots that he can normally make from the floor," Thunder coach Mark Daigneault said of Wembanyama. "I thought Chet did a great job on him. I thought Mara did a great job on him in the possessions he had him. There's been times where we could get a little jumpy with him and we overhelp and give up something clean. There's other times where we've left him on an island. I thought tonight we had the perfect balance of providing help, putting him in a crowd, discipline on the ball, but not hemorrhaging in other parts of the floor." Spurs coach Mitch Johnson declined to single out Wembanyama's shaky performance. Oklahoma City jumped out to a 26-point lead in the second quarter, shooting a scorching 10-of-14 from 3-point range in the first half as San Antonio struggled to find its way offensively with a new guard-heavy starting lineup that featured Wembanyama and Fox with Dylan Harper , Stephon Castle and Devin Vassell . "I think everybody struggled pretty equally," Johnson said when asked about Wembanyama. "I know his field goal [percentage] will stand out, but we all participated in that one." Fox agreed, pointing out that San Antonio's guards need to find ways to make Wembanyama's job easier. "There are times we want to play faster, try to make his catches a little easier to where he doesn't have to always create from himself," Fox said. "Whenever he's able to get those easy baskets, then you see the highlight plays. If we can make it just a little bit easier for him, I think that's when you start seeing the 40, 45 points, the step-back 3s. That's when those things will happen." Castle said San Antonio's guards need to find ways to deliver the ball to Wembanyama in better spots on the floor. "When we screen for him, [we have to] make sure we get his guy off of him," Castle said. "He had a bad shooting night, but he did a good job of getting to the rim. He turned a couple shots that he usually shoots down to make a play for other people. It was the first game of the season. We all know Vic will find his rhythm. That's not something we're really worried about." ESPN's Tim MacMahon and ESPN Research contributed to this report.

stories.title: Former Cowboys DB, Broncos scout Cornell Green dies at 86
stories.summary: The Cowboys announced that former defensive back Cornell Green died Wednesday.
stories.detailText: The Cowboys announced that former defensive back Cornell Green died Wednesday . He was 86. Green grew up in California as an elite basketball player, earning all-start honors. He went to Utah State, where he earned All-America honors in 1961 and '62. His 1,067 rebounds still stand as the school's career record, and he is Utah State's sixth-leading scorer with 1,890 points. He had planned to join the NBA after the Chicago Zephyrs drafted him in 1962, but the Cowboys offered Green an invite to training camp. Despite only one year of football experience — his junior year of high school — Green made the Cowboys' roster. Green never missed a game over the next 13 seasons, starting 167 of 168 games after his rookie season. He played cornerback his first eight seasons. Green led the Cowboys in interceptions four times, earned three Pro Bowl invites and garnered two first-team All-Pro honors. In 1970, Green moved to safety, where he was named a Pro Bowler again in 1971 and '72. He played in two NFL Championship Games and Super Bowl V before helping the Cowboys win the Lombardi Trophy with a 24-3 victory over the Dolphins in Super Bowl VI. Green retired after the 1974 season and went into scouting. He worked for the Cowboys and Broncos, earning NFL Scout of the Year in 2010. Green's 34 career interceptions are tied for fifth in the team record book.

stories.title: Bucs list QB Baker Mayfield as full participant, WR Emeka Egbuka with concussion after first practice of Week 7
stories.summary: Mayfield returned to practice for the first time since dislocating the thumb on his throwing hand in a Week 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
stories.detailText: On Wednesday, Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield practiced for the first time since dislocating the thumb on his throwing hand in a Week 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings . More specifically, Mayfield was a full participant, according to the team’s injury report , which also revealed that wide receiver Emeka Egbuka is dealing with a concussion as the Buccaneers gear up for a Week 7 road game versus the Carolina Panthers. Head coach Todd Bowles told reporters that Mayfield is “coming along fine.” “I think once he got warmed up, it started looking pretty good as practice went on,” Bowles said. “So we'll continue to monitor and see how he goes through the week.” Later, Bowles was asked when he anticipates making the call on Mayfield possibly playing against the Panthers on Sunday. “I’ll see what he looks like Friday, and I’ll find out then,” the fifth-year Bucs frontman said. Week 7 Injury Report (10/21/26) - Tampa Bay @Buccaneers at Carolina Panthers: https://t.co/vcQCXz5IWt #WeAreTheKrewe pic.twitter.com/vk2Rujx8HK — Buccaneers Communications (@BuccaneersComms) October 21, 2026 Mayfield wore a glove on his throwing hand throughout the entirety of Wednesday’s practice, Bowles confirmed. Bowles said Mayfield told him it felt fine and that he’s done it once before. The two-time Pro Bowler’s return has hinged on his ability to properly grip the football following the injury he sustained on the follow-through of an interception he tossed against the Vikings . At first, a three-week absence was expected, but then an ESPN report surfaced on Oct. 4 that suggested Mayfield could be sidelined up to six weeks . So the three-week timeline reportedly was the best-case scenario for the Bucs. Now 1-5, Tampa Bay is fortunate that Mayfield’s recovery may be unfolding that way. Bowles explained, though, that the Bucs will have to take a wait-and-see approach to this week. “We got to see how he comes out of it and, after a day, how the thumb responds,” he said. Both Mayfield and backup Jalon Daniels understand the game plan and are preparing, Bowles noted, when asked about splitting the reps between them. Bowles also mentioned that it was encouraging to see Mayfield do the things the Tampa Bay staff wanted him to do on Wednesday. Mayfield dealt with an array of injuries amid the 2025 season, most notably one to his non-throwing shoulder last November. He played banged up, suiting up for all 17 games of the Bucs’ 8-9 campaign. A reporter inquired Wednesday about how Bowles and Co. will weigh sending Mayfield out there if he’s not 100%. “I think it's a different injury,” Bowles said. “This one's a thumb. You can kind of gauge it off how he throws and how he feels and how he takes snaps under center and how he feels afterwards. I think that's kind of a different deal than the shoulder and the bruises and all those things he's kind of added up to. “This one you can see flat out, and you can know whether you want to play him or not.” If Mayfield isn’t ready to go for Sunday’s game, Daniels will continue to start in his place. The undrafted rookie quarterbacked Tampa Bay to a “Thursday Night Football” win over the Dallas Cowboys in his second career start. Daniels, who appeared in 49 games across six seasons at Kansas, has completed 61.2% of his passes over his first four outings with the Bucs. He’s thrown for 501 yards, ran for 126 more and posted a 3:5 touchdown-to-interception ratio and 1-2 record along the way. He and Tampa Bay blew a 13-point fourth-quarter lead to the Pittsburgh Steelers last week and wound up losing in overtime .

stories.title: Why we should continue rooting for the Cowboys to turn things around
stories.summary: There is a lot riding on this season for the Cowboys.
stories.detailText: Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys had Super Bowl aspirations entering the 2026 NFL season and that shouldn’t change despite their overall poor play to start the year, which has resulted in a 2-4 record through the first six weeks. This is a team that has the talent to turn things around and every reason to do so due to the unique situation they find themselves in. First off, the Cowboys are still very much in the playoff race due to the poor state of the NFC East division. For the second week in a row, all four teams in the NFC East failed to win, leaving the division up for grabs. Despite disappointing at every turn so for this year, Dallas is still somehow considered the favorite by many to be the division champs. As long as their playoff hopes are still alive, we can fully expect Jerry Jones and Company to do everything within their power to turn things around. That means another big trade could be in play before the November 10 deadline as well as them sticking with and remaining patient with Brian Schottenheimer, despite his questionable coaching/decision-making. As much as many of us would like to see Schottenheimer replaced after his many coaching gaffs, that seems highly unlikely given the state of the NFC East division and the possibility of the Cowboys coming out on top. After all, who would step in to replace him? Klayton Adams? He is supposedly an up-and-coming HC candidate, but even he’s an unproven one. Another reason to keep rooting for the Cowboys to turn things around and finish strong has to do with draft positioning. They currently hold two first-round selections in the 2027 NFL Draft, but the higher of the two belongs to the New York Jets as part of the trade package for Quinnen Williams. As things stand right now that would be the sixth and 27 th overall picks, the latter of which is from the Green Bay Packers for Micah Parsons. How the Packers end the things is completely out of the Cowboys control. They could continue to string wins together, make the playoffs, or perhaps even the Super Bowl. That would put their first-round pick in the latter part of the round. What they can control is how they finish the season, preferably as a playoff team or even better as a Super Bowl champion. That way the difference between the Cowboys and Packers first-round picks is minimal at best. No one wants to see the Cowboys part with a Top 10 selection as things currently stand. That would just be rubbing salt in an open, festering wound after suffering through in another disappointing season. That would be the ultimate gut punch. While the Cowboys may be disappointing us at nearly every turn so for this year, there is still reason to root for them to turn things around and finish strong. All of the pieces, at least most of them, seem to be in place. It’s up to them to start executing and playing better. For the sake for mental health, all of us are probably hoping they can do so. Where are you on the season? Have you packed it in already? Or are you rooting for the turnaround?

stories.title: Panthers LB Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) set to miss Week 7 game vs. Bucs
stories.summary: Panthers coach Dave Canales said the team is preparing to host the Buccaneers on Sunday without top outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips.
stories.detailText: CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Carolina Panthers coach Dave Canales said Wednesday the team is preparing to host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday without top outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips . Canales didn't offer a timeline for Phillips (hamstring) to return, but he avoided any gamesmanship on Phillips' status for Week 7. When asked if the expectation was that Phillips would miss this week, with a Thursday Night Football matchup against the Green Bay Packers on deck for Week 8, Canales noted that Phillips, who reinjured his left injury hamstring in the win over the Philadelphia Eagles , needed to be treated with caution. "I think I can fairly say that," Canales said about Phillips missing Week 7. "I know there are advantages to game plans, but this is something that we need to address and take care of." Phillips left Sunday's win in the first half but returned late in the third quarter. On Wednesday, Phillips walked around the perimeter of the Panthers' practice field while his teammates participated in a walkthrough. "Jaelan got that same hamstring [injury] -- we've got to take care of that now," Canales said. "So, we're going to still push it and evaluate him, but this is something we're going to have to be smart with. Two weeks off of the first injury and then he was able to finish the game, which was incredible for him to go back out there and do his job. But the MRIs, the findings, this is something that we're going to have to treat more intensively." Phillips, who signed a four-year, $120 million deal in March, has produced 2.5 sacks on the season. The former Miami Dolphins and Eagles pass rusher was brought in, along with inside linebacker Devin Lloyd , to turn around a middling Carolina defense. But this Sunday, like Lloyd in Week 3's loss to the Cleveland Browns , Phillips will need to watch from the sideline as he recovers from injury. Canales declined to speculate whether Phillips would be able to play at Green Bay next week. For now, though, with Phillips and special teams ace Thomas Incoom (calf) sidelined, the Panthers plan to call up practice squad linebacker Nick Hampton. The former Los Angeles Rams pass rusher is known for his special teams ability, and he recently returned to the Panthers after being cut with an undisclosed injury during training camp "It's the reason why we brought him back, and he was having a great camp before he had the injury," Canales said. "So, we're excited to see Nick this week, and then some of the other guys that we've been working with, they've got to be ready if we go that direction with more guys." Incoom, according to Canales, is considered week-to-week and won't be immediately placed on injured reserve. Incoom was injured against the Eagles and Canales said it took four players to fill his role on special teams throughout the remainder of the Week 6 win. Along with Phillips and Incoom, running back Chuba Hubbard , right tackle Taylor Moton and tight ends Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller were given veteran rest days. Running back AJ Dillon (ankle) and offensive tackle Monroe Freeling (knee) were full participants after missing the previous week of practice and the win over the Eagles. Quarterback Bryce Young (knee) was on the injury report, but he was a full participant as in previous weeks.

stories.title: Ravens' Lamar Jackson returns to practice but status remains unclear vs. Bengals
stories.summary: After practice, Jackson was favoring his injured left ankle, walking into the team facility with a noticeable limp.
stories.detailText: OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson returned to practice Wednesday, but it remains uncertain whether the two-time NFL Most Valuable Player will play in Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals . After practice, Jackson was favoring his injured left ankle, walking into the team facility with a noticeable limp. He also walked with a limp inside the locker room. Jackson wasn't present during the media availability portion of practice, but he later came out onto the practice field. This marked the first time that Jackson has had any on-field work since spraining his ankle 17 days ago. Ravens coach Jesse Minter described Jackson as a limited participant, saying he "was able to get in a little bit of work and be involved in preparation." Minter also indicated Jackson participated in some team drills. "There's nobody that wants to be out there more than Lamar," Minter said. "Lamar wants to play. But at the same time, you got to be healthy enough to play." Jackson sprained his left ankle late in the first half of a 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans on Oct. 4. He had missed the past two games and the past six practices before returning Wednesday. Tyler Huntley has filled in for Jackson, leading the Ravens to a comeback win at the Atlanta Falcons before struggling Sunday in a loss at the Cleveland Browns . In 14 quarters with Jackson this season, the Ravens have scored 116 points and 14 offensive touchdowns. In 10 quarters without him, Baltimore has totaled 40 points and four touchdowns. "He is working to get back," Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers said. "He is working every day, doing what he needs to do to get back on the field. That's all you can do when you're injured, just do everything you can to get back on the field." If Jackson can play Sunday, it would be a timely return. The Ravens (4-2) and the Bengals (3-2) are considered the top two teams in the AFC North. Since Jackson became the starter midway through the 2018 season, the Ravens are 11-2 against the Bengals with Jackson, who has thrown 24 touchdowns and six interceptions against Cincinnati. Without Jackson over that span, Baltimore is 0-3, including the playoffs, against the Bengals, losing by an average margin of 12 points. "I know this, that when it's ready for him to be able to play and we feel like that's the best thing to do, that's what we'll do," Minter said.

stories.title: Jameis Winston on losing his starting job: I understand where I am now
stories.summary: The Giants benched Jameis Winston just 23 days after trading with the Vikings for J.J.
stories.detailText: The Giants benched Jameis Winston just 23 days after trading with the Vikings for J.J. McCarthy. McCarthy will become the third quarterback to start for the Giants, following Jaxson Dart and Winston. Dart tore the MCL and meniscus in his left knee in Week 2, ending his season. Winston started the past four games, going 2-1-1. He was only 14-of-26 for 152 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions on Sunday, leaving with the Giants trailing 34-10 in the fourth quarter. McCarthy rallied the team, going 11-of-21 for 243 yards, a touchdown and an interception and gave the Giants a chance for a miracle comeback. That's why Winston accepts returning to a backup role. "Last game it wasn’t what it was capble of being," Winston said, via video from SNY Giants. "Every single week, you're defined off of the last time you stepped foot on the field. So I believe based off last game, my job is to lead the New York Football Giants to a win, and that didn't happen. That being said, I understand where I am now." Winston has spent most of the past seven seasons as a backup, so he's familiar with the role. "Just focusing on one day at a time," Winston said. "I'm extremely grateful that I still get to do what I love, and that's play football at a high level for the New York Football Giants. Being able to accept roles and understand like, 'What is your significant role? How can I be the best at my role with this team?' is one of the things you have to adjust to in this league."

stories.summary: One more thing to root against this Sunday.
stories.detailText: Sunday will be the first chance for the Cincinnati Bengals to face former pass rusher Trey Hendrickson. One of Hendrickson’s Baltimore Ravens teammates is drinking the Kool-Aid on this revenge game with a pretty big prediction: “Trey is a great leader, and he’s a guy who flies around,” linebacker Trenton Simpson said Wednesday. “And man, I am excited to see him against his former team. The things he’s doing in practice, the way he rushed the passer, and just how he’d get off the ball. And I believe that this game for him is about to be like one of those multiple-sack games. So I’m calling it. I’m excited to see the celebration he does, so I’m excited.” Ravens linebacker Trenton Simpson is predicting a multi-sack game for Trey Hendrickson, who is facing his former team in the Bengals. “I’m calling it,” Simpson said. pic.twitter.com/r02Sdm3p0p — Jamison Hensley (@jamisonhensley) October 21, 2026 Hendrickson has missed two games this season with a broken finger that he got surgery on. If he were to have multiple sacks, it would be the first such performance with Baltimore, as he only has two sacks so far. He looked good last week against the Cleveland Browns, getting plenty of pressure on a rookie left tackle and recording a sack. It will be interesting to see how the Bengals scheme up pass protection with Hendrickson. One thing we know is the team will likely be excited to run directly at him. For years, one of the biggest knocks was that you could run at Hendrickson and gain yards pretty easily. It became more obvious as the defense deteriorated around him There is no doubt Hendrickson will be wearing the biggest chip on his shoulder. He was loud and clear about his displeasure with the front office, and he’d tell anyone who would listen about his offseason contract drama. That has clearly left a bad taste in most fans’ mouths. Now, the Bengals will need to keep Hendrickson from having a big day if they are to come out of Baltimore with a W.

Sills, 28, has played in 21 games for the Colts and Philadelphia Eagles since 2022. He is a former undrafted free agent. Sills has played 41 offensive and 79 special teams snaps. The move was necessitated by injuries at the tackle position. The team’s top three tackles — Andrew Thomas (groin), Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), and Marcus Mbow missed practice on Wednesday. Thomas has been managing his groin injury since Week 2. He has played in each game since despite practicing sparingly. Eluemunor missed last week’s game. Mbow, Eluemunor’s replacement, appeared to suffer an injury late in Sunday’s game against the New Orleans Saints. He is on the injury report with a knee issue. Other than Sills, the only healthy tackle on the roster is rookie J.C. Davis. Davis saw his first game action last Sunday in relief of Thomas during the fourth quarter. Also of concern on the injury report, starting safety Jevon Holland and starting cornerback Greg Newsome II have concussions, and starting inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds missed Wednesday’s practice with a shoulder injury. stories.title: Bears RB Kyle Monangai (toe, thumb) out Thursday vs. Patriots
stories.summary: The Bears have ruled RB Kyle Monangai out for Thursday night's matchup against the Patriots with lingering toe and thumb injuries.
stories.detailText: CHICAGO -- The Bears will be without running back Kyle Monangai against the New England Patriots in Week 7. Monangai did not practice in any of the Bears walk-throughs ahead of Thursday night's game at Soldier Field and is set to miss his third straight game with turf toe and thumb injuries. The Bears lead the NFL with 161 rushing yards per game but were held below 100 in consecutive games with Monangai sidelined. The former seventh rounder is averaging 5.4 yards per rush, which is the fourth most in the NFL behind Kenneth Walker III (6.3), Bijan Robinson (5.8) and Jaylen Warren (5.5). Chicago was averaging 6.8 yards per play with Monangai on the field, a figure that has dipped to 4.7 without him. Monangai produced a career-high 30 carries for 146 yards and two touchdowns in the Bears' 23-12 win over the Jets in Week 4. He exited that game late in the fourth quarter with a thumb injury, but it wasn't until the following week that he appeared on the injury report with a toe injury. Coach Ben Johnson said Monangai's toe injury was a "bigger deal" than the team initially anticipated, which prompted a visit to a specialist for further evaluation. The running back was then categorized by Johnson as "week-to-week." Last Friday, Johnson intimated that the Monangai's absence should not be longer than four games, the mandated amount a player would miss with an injured reserve designation. "It wasn't one of those things we felt like we needed to put him on IR for," Johnson said on Oct.16. "So, it's still week to week and as far as I know, he's trending in the right direction." In five of its six games, New England has had held opponents below 100 rushing yards.

stories.title: Roger Goodell: NFL is "comfortable" with Steve Tisch participating in league, team activities
stories.summary: Steve Tisch supposedly has given up his ownership interest in the Giants.
stories.detailText: {"unknownError":"There has been an error","expiredError":"This video has been expired due to copyright restrictions.","unavailableError":"This content is not yet available.","georestrictedError":"This content is not available in your location.","networkId":"169843","adManagerUrl":"https://mssl.fwmrm.net/libs/adm/6.51.0/AdManager.js","serverId":"https://29773.v.fwmrm.net/ad/g/1","profileId":"169843:nbcu_web_jwp_cs_moat_https","afid":"140315314","caid":"nbcs_nbc_pft_teamdoctors_261021","csid":"nbcsports_embed_on_domain","sfid":"","adHocGroup":"","athlete":"","businessUnit":"NBC Sports","category":"","duration":"430697","event":"","externalAdvertiserId":"nbcs_nbc_pft_teamdoctors_261021","genre":"News","guid":"nbc_pft_teamdoctors_261021","league":"NFL","network":"","platform":"PC","playlist":"","show":"ProFootballTalk","sport":"Football","subtype":"","team":"Philadelphia Eagles","title": "How ‘unaffiliated’ doctors can help in the NFL","datePublished":"","videoPageUrl": "https://www.nbcsports.com/watch/nfl/profootballtalk/how-unaffiliated-doctors-can-help-in-situations-like-jalen-hurts","availableDate":"2026-10-21T12:30:09Z","expirationDate":"","countries":""} Steve Tisch supposedly has given up his ownership interest in the Giants. He's still acting as if he partially owns the team. And the NFL is fine with that. On Wednesday, Commissioner Roger Goodell was asked about Tisch's presence at the NFL's quarterly ownership meetings. "I think we're comfortable with him participating as the Giants suggest," Goodell said. Although Tisch no longer holds equity in Giants (his interest was transferred to his children's trust), he continues to serve as te team's chairman of the board. He was present in the team's draft room. He has been at games. Tisch's role came into question once the Epstein files revealed a series of emails between Tisch and Jeffrey Epstein. Subsequent reporting raised questions regarding whether Epstein was arranging dates for Tisch, and whether Tisch was possibly using his influence in the film industry to leverage an exchange of favors . Goodell, in March, cited Tisch's exit from ownership when discussing the NFL's investigation of Tisch. Goodell has repeatedly said it has no evidence of wrongdoing by Tisch. There's no evidence, however, that the NFL has attempted to gather any such evidence. It's possible the league simply hoped to run out the clock and wait for the topic to change. As it often does. Regarding Tisch, the league hasn't done anything. At this point, it likely won't. The emails alone were enough to get the league to nudge Tisch to the sideline. The league, Tisch, and the Giants seemed to believe that Tisch giving to his children now the equity they would have inevitably inherited was enough to end the issue. As long as Tisch continues to be conspicuous when it comes to league and team events, the issue remains.

stories.title: Patriots at Bears Q&A: The Battle of 2024 QB Supremacy
stories.summary: The Chicago Bears welcome the New England Patriots on Thursday. We sat down with Pats Pulpit (SB Nation’s Patriots site) to get you set for the matchup.
stories.detailText: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 10: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears and Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots interact after a game at Soldier Field on November 10, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. The Patriots defeated the Bears 19-3. (Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Bears have a quick turnaround this week, playing Thursday night against the New England Patriots. Both the Patriots and Bears are playing good football right now as they both sit at 4-2. The last time these two teams played was in 2024. A game where the Bears’ offense looked so inept that it ended with the firing of Shane Waldron. The Bears are in a much different place heading into this matchup, and the Patriots are looking like an AFC playoff team following up their Super Bowl appearance in February. To get you set for this big game, we sat down with Taylor Kyles from Pat’s Pulpit (SB Nation’s New England Patriots site) to get you a better perspective of where the Patriots are at. Here’s that Q&A. 1. We know the big topic of this game is going to be the battle of 2024 first-round QBs. Caleb Williams has beaten all his first-round QB-mates except for Bo Nix (hasn’t played him) and Drake Maye after the disastrous game in 2024 that led to Shane Waldron being fired. Are there any lingering concerns about Drake Maye’s poor stretch of play, or is confidence high that he’s all the way back? Drake Maye has done a complete 180 since his ugly three-game stretch to start the season. Through that initial rough patch, Maye was putting the ball in harm’s way due to poor decision-making, and that seemed to shake his confidence and affect his fundamentals. But since turning things around in Buffalo, Maye has returned to MVP-caliber form and done an excellent job maximizing his arm talent and mobility. One of the best examples is his deep passing, where he went from a 0-4 touchdown-to-interception ratio from Weeks 1-3 to a 5-0 ratio from Weeks 4-6, the best mark in the league over that span. Between his improved sense of risk-vs-reward, ability to avoid potential negative plays, and impressive field vision, I think it’s safe to say early concerns have been put to bed. That said, Maye must prove he can replicate this dominance and ball security against the league’s best defenses. 2. The offensive line for New England certainly looks significantly beat up, and I’m sure the short week doesn’t help. How much of an issue is this for the Patriots? C Jared Wilson is the only Patriots lineman to play ever snap for the offense, excluding garbage time. RG Mike Onwenu is on injured reserve with an ankle injury; RT Morgan Moses has dealt with a foot injury for weeks; LT Will Campbell was knocked out of Week 5’s Raiders game with a knee injury; and LG Alijah Vera-Tucker left last week’s Jets game with a hamstring injury. Even Onwenu’s backup Ben Brown, who’d been playing well for a natural center, was knocked out last week with a knee injury. Campbell looked good last week despite his recent injury, and Moses should play on Thursday night, but the Patriots will be starting reserves on the attack: Matt Pryor and LG Walter Rouse. Pryor is a big, powerful veteran who didn’t give up pressure and generated movement in the ground game, but his lateral quickness is lacking, and he struggled to sustain blocks in the ground game. Rouse flashed as a run blocker, but didn’t get any quality pass protection snaps and struggled in that area when he was asked to step in late against the Jaguars. If I’m the Bears, I’m targeting the interior on blitzes and stunts to force a group without much experience together to communicate and be on the same page, specifically to the offense’s left. 3. Can you give us one player on offense and one player on defense that Bears fans may not know but you think can make a significant impact on Thursday night? WR Kyle Williams has been a bit of a one-trick pony for the Patriots since being drafted in the third round last year, but that one trick is catching go-balls for touchdowns. Williams has an excellent release package and the speed to hit home runs at any moment, especially with Maye throwing him the ball. Williams is expected to have a bigger role with Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins on injured reserve, and he could be a difference-maker given how shaky the Bears’ outside corners have been defending the deep ball. On defense, Elijah Ponder looks like a rising star one year after joining the Patriots as an undrafted free agent, tying for third in the NFL with 5.5 sacks. He’s a big edge defender with the explosiveness and bend of someone much smaller, and he’s provided quality play as a pass rusher, run defender, and occasional coverage player. Ponder beat tackles one-on-one, even if his technique is still a work in progress, but last week he showed he can also win and free up teammates on stunts. I wouldn’t be surprised if he makes it a long night for LT Theo Benedet. 4. What happened to AJ Brown last week? I’m sure he was rusty, but that seemed like someone coated his hands in butter before the game. Any concerns about his performance moving forward for New England? A.J. Brown’s drops were ugly, and they even extended to the onside kick recovery team, where he almost gave the Jets a chance to come back late in the game. That said, he was open on nearly all of his targets, and the egregiousness of his drops led me to believe the receiver was in his head after missing four games with a high ankle sprain. Brown is a professional and one of the best pass-catchers on the planet, so I won’t be worried unless the issue becomes an unshakable habit. 5. How do you think this Super Bowl XX rematch plays out (Sorry, I had to bring it up, you understand)? As a native Chicagoan, I can let that one slide. And there’s no shame in losing to the ‘85 Bears (Rest in peace, Coach Ditka)! I see this game being close early before turning into a good old-fashioned shootout with Drake Maye and Caleb Williams showing why they’re two of the league’s top young talents. I’m predicting Andy Borragales pays off a long drive from Maye and company to win 31-28.

stories.title: Patriots' Alijah Vera-Tucker, Ben Brown ruled out vs. Bears
stories.summary: The Patriots will be without starting guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown for Thursday's game against the Bears due to injuries, coach Mike Vrabel said.
stories.detailText: FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- The New England Patriots will be without starting guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown for Thursday's road game against the Chicago Bears due to injuries, coach Mike Vrabel said. Vera-Tucker played every snap this season at left guard before injuring his hamstring in the second quarter of Sunday's win over the visiting New York Jets , his former team. Brown, meanwhile, was the third right guard to start -- after Mike Onwenu and Greg Van Roten both landed on injured reserve -- and he hobbled off in the second half of Sunday's game with a knee injury. Vrabel said Walter Rouse , a three-year veteran acquired in a trade from the Minnesota Vikings on Aug. 30, will start at left guard. It will be his first career NFL start. Vrabel said nine-year veteran Matt Pryor , whom the Patriots signed off the Arizona Cardinals ' practice squad Oct. 1, will start at right guard. He has started 40 career games, with 15 of them coming in the 2024 season with the Bears. Quarterback Drake Maye wasn't sacked in Sunday's win, and he credited the offensive line -- which also played without veteran right tackle Morgan Moses (foot) for two-plus quarters -- for exemplary work. "I feel like it's been every week somebody stepping up," Maye said. "On the flip side of it, it's unfortunate seeing so many of our guys go down. I'm impressed with how the coaches have been handling it, of kind of moving personnel around and fixing things on the sideline and adjusting." Moses was limited in practice in recent days, but Vrabel said he has a chance to play against the Bears. The Patriots (4-2), who also placed starting receiver Romeo Doubs (shoulder) on injured reserve Monday and will be without starting cornerback Carlton Davis III (neck) for the third game in a row, have won three straight games.

stories.title: Seahawks never offered Kenneth Walker a contract before free agency
stories.summary: A new report changes the story behind Seattle’s decision to let its Super Bowl MVP walk.
stories.detailText: The Seattle Seahawks’ decision to let Kenneth Walker III leave in free agency has been one of the most debated moves of their offseason. With the former Super Bowl MVP thriving with the Kansas City Chiefs and Seattle struggling to establish a consistent running game, the conversation has often centered on the team’s decision to retain Rashid Shaheed rather than bring Walker back. But according to a new report, that debate might have been built on the wrong premise: the Seahawks never even made Walker a contract offer. In a report for The Athletic , Mike Dugar revealed that Seattle did not engage in serious discussions about bringing Walker back before free agency. There were no serious discussions — on that day or any other — about Walker returning to the team that used a second-round draft pick on him in 2022. Walker’s postseason performance put him in such high demand that he effectively priced himself out of Seattle, which didn’t make a contract offer ahead of free agency, according to league sources not authorized to speak publicly about the matter. That revelation changes the context surrounding one of general manager John Schneider’s most scrutinized offseason decisions. Rather than a straightforward choice between paying Walker and investing in Shaheed, the report suggests Seattle never formally attempted to retain its starting running back. The Seahawks never made an offer to their Super Bowl MVP Walker’s departure was not entirely unexpected for the RB. The fourth-year running back had just completed a postseason run that transformed his standing around the league, finishing with 135 rushing yards in Seattle’s Super Bowl victory over the New England Patriots and earning MVP honors . His regular-season production was great, too. Walker rushed for 1,027 yards in 2025, although his role was shared with Zach Charbonnet, who scored 12 rushing touchdowns compared to Walker’s five. When Charbonnet suffered a torn ACL during the divisional-round win over the San Francisco 49ers, Walker became Seattle’s primary option and delivered 313 rushing yards and four touchdowns across the team’s final three playoff games. That performance helped establish his value heading into free agency. The Chiefs ultimately signed Walker to a three-year, $43 million contract, making him one of the highest-paid running backs in the NFL. Walker had already suggested that he knew his time in Seattle was coming to an end. Speaking to Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk in May, he explained that he had realized during the season that a return was unlikely. “Things ain’t work out how I was expecting it to, and that’s all right,” Walker said. “It worked out for the team. But yeah, (I knew) sometime during the season, and then we get to free agency, you pretty much know you weren’t going to be there.” The report also revisits the awkward moment during Seattle’s Super Bowl celebration when Schneider joked that Walker had tried negotiating a contract with him moments before taking the stage. Walker subsequently denied that account on Instagram, and Schneider later described the incident as a “panic moment.” As Dugar’s reporting now makes clear, there were no serious contract negotiations behind the joke. Kenneth Walker gets his chance to remind Seattle what it lost The timing of Dugar’s report could hardly be more significant. On Sunday, Walker will return to Lumen Field for the first time as an opponent when the Seahawks host the Chiefs on Sunday Night Football . His first season in Kansas City has been spectacular. Walker has rushed for 665 yards and six touchdowns in five games, leading the NFL in rushing yards at the time of Dugar’s report. He has also helped transform the Chiefs’ ground game into one of the league’s most productive units, giving Patrick Mahomes another way to punish defenses that focus too heavily on the passing attack. Seattle, meanwhile, has struggled to find that same balance. Its running backs have combined for 539 yards and three touchdowns, according to The Athletic , despite Walker producing more yardage individually while playing one fewer game. Injuries have contributed to the problem, including a chest issue that sent rookie Jadarian Price to injured reserve, but the contrast remains striking. The matchup will also present a major test for Seattle’s defense. The Seahawks have established themselves as one of the league’s strongest units against the run, and they will attempt to contain a player who knows the organization, its personnel and its home stadium intimately. Walker enters the game averaging 133 rushing yards per contest, making him a formidable challenge for a defense that has not allowed an opposing running back to reach 100 rushing yards since Week 8 of the 2024 season. For Walker, Sunday is an opportunity to demonstrate just how much his role has changed. In Seattle, he shared opportunities with Charbonnet and never received a contract offer that would have kept him with the franchise. In Kansas City, he has become a central piece of an offense built to maximize his explosive running ability. For the Seahawks, the reunion will bring renewed attention to a decision that looked increasingly questionable as the season progressed. That makes Sunday’s matchup more than a reunion with a former player. It is a chance for Walker to show Seattle what it is missing — and for the Seahawks to confront the consequences of an offseason decision that, according to the latest report, was made without even putting a contract offer on the table.

stories.title: Patriots decide on starting guard duo against Bears
stories.summary: The Patriots will be without Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown on Thursday night.
stories.detailText: The New England Patriots will be without both of their starting guards on Thursday against the Chicago Bears, but they have already decided on who will replace them. As head coach Mike Vrabel announced on Wednesday, Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor will fill the two vacant spots in the lineup. “We have a lot of consideration. We go through things, different scenarios,” Vrabel explained during a press conference at Gillette Stadium. “We’re going to go with where we finished on Sunday and see what that looks like, and then have everybody else ready to go.” Rouse and Pryor started Sunday’s game against the New York Jets on the bench, but were forced into action due to the injuries suffered higher up on the depth chart. Pryor was first up, entering at right guard in the second quarter after Alijah Vera-Tucker left with a hamstring injury. With Ben Brown sliding over to Vera-Tucker’s spot, the 31-year-old took the field for his first offensive snaps since arriving in Foxborough. He finished the game with 46 snaps . Rouse entered the mix in the fourth quarter, after Brown went out with a knee injury. He played the final 14 offensive snaps of the day. The 25-year-old had previously played extended snaps albeit at right guard during the Patriots’ Week 3 loss in Jacksonville; in that game, Rouse was the backup at that particular position and called upon after Greg Van Roten — himself an injury replacement for regular starter Mike Onwenu — was lost to injury. Now, the two will be part of the starting lineup against the Bears. The group will also consist of left tackle Will Campbell and center Jared Wilson. Right tackle Morgan Moses is officially questionable because of a foot injury, with first-round rookie Caleb Lomu a candidate to enter the lineup if need be. Earlier this week, Mike Vrabel said that the Patriots need Lomu to be “ready to go at multiple positions” versus the Bears. Kickoff between the two teams is scheduled for 8:15 p.m. ET on Thursday.
