(Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images A lot of the talk now is about the trade deadline. Many folks are speculating what the Vikings should do. Some fans prefer they stand pat and save the draft capital and cap space. This is not a bad idea. Since the Colts look to be in free fall, speculation abounds about them moving some of their top players like Quentin Nelson and DeForest Buckner. Both would be fabulous pickups for the Vikings. I like Jonathan Taylor myself due to the fact that Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason are both free agents next year and, more importantly, Taylor would be under contract for two more years with none guaranteed, He would be due 16 & 18M the next two years. Nelson and Buckner will be free agents and will get paid well is my guess. Some folks have speculated about the Vikings trying to trade for Ben Bredeson of the Bucs but he is their starter so it is hard to see that happening. They need to protect Baker. It is hard to find a decent guard that might be available. Nelson would be the crown jewel but that would mean an immediate extension and moving Jackson to right guard. Not sure about that. Buckner could be the extra squeeze to get the defense more juice that the team needs. He has a 74.9 pass-rushing pff grade which ranks 12th overall showing he still has elite pass-rush efficiency. He has already racked up 4 sacks and 18 total pressures (including 3 hits and 9 hurries). If the Colts are sellers, they probably are going to move Nelson and Buckner who likely want to go to a team that has a chance to get into the dance no? Who do you think the team could and will sign? Minnesota Vikings News and Links NFL Power Rankings: Vikings Status After Week 6 Bye https://www.vikings.com/news/nfl-power-rankings-week-7-status-bye-week No. 3 (no change): Gary Davenport – Bleacher Report There isn’t a more surprising team in the NFL this year (at least in a positive way) than the undefeated Minnesota Vikings. Naysayers will point to a relatively easy schedule and offensive inconsistency as reasons why they aren’t as good their record. But Minnesota’s ultra-aggressive defense is legit: second in yards allowed, third against the pass, fifth against the run and first in points allowed. Edge-rusher Andrew Van Ginkel told reporters the defense’s strength lies in its versatility. “Things are constantly changing,” he said. “It could be changing game to game. It could be changing from series to series. It could be changing from play to play. It could be changing within the play.” That defense is going to be tested coming up — after facing the struggling Colts at home in Week 7, the Vikings take on two of the league’s best offenses in the Lions and Bills. No. 3 (up 1 spot): Vinnie Iyer – Sporting News The Vikings defense has been the foundation of their undefeated start through their Week 6 bye. They have impressive pressure and takeaway stats in Brian Flores’ aggressive, blitz-happy attack, but there’s one simple number for why they haven’t lost. Their defense allows opponents to convert only a league-best 22 percent of third-down attempts. No. 5 (up 2 spots): Frank Schwab – Yahoo! Sports Jordan Mason’s return from a broken thumb, which should happen in Week 7, won’t create big headlines, but it’s important for the Vikings. Aaron Jones, Sr., filled in well, but he’s 31 years old, and asking him to handle almost all of the running back duties was not a long-term plan. Mason and Jones form a good committee, and they can resume their roles. The Vikings face the reeling Colts this weekend before a four-game stretch that will define their season: at Lions, vs. Bills, at Packers, vs. 49ers (in Mexico City). If they beat the Colts and go 2-2 in the four games that follow, they’ll be in great shape. Offensive coordinator Wes Phillips talked about that coming out of the bye week and was open about how much Murray tried to acclimate. “There wasn’t any like resistance or like, ‘Hey, I don’t want to do any of this stuff’; it was, it was more like, ‘Hey, I want to do what you guys, your offense is,’ and us trying to adjust some to make sure that he’s comfortable, but he was very open right from the start,” said Phillips. You can see how that’s evolved over the last few weeks, especially with how much Murray was under center against the Buccaneers. They have significantly increased the shotgun percentage with the offense, and it’s done a lot for how successful they’ve been able to be. To Murray’s credit, it’s not as if he can’t play under center; he did that with the Cardinals the last three years under Drew Petzing. He has played under center. They’re trying to figure out our system, and then they start opening up and saying, okay, have you ever done it this way? And the communication with him and the play caller, Kevin, has just grown and grown as we’ve gone, as you’d expect it to, you know, as we get through our first year with him.” Vikings Trade Rumors Hint at Potential Moves Before Deadline https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/vikings-trade-rumors-hint-potential-032756253.html “On The Alec Lewis Show, he tripled down on his reports from KFAN and The Athletic earlier in the week, telling his YouTube and podcast audience that the MN Vikings will be ‘very active and aggressive’ in trying to find trade partners before the deadline.. Lewis even adding that he’s more “convicted and confident” a deal will get done this year than he has been the past couple seasons, before Teasley arrived as general manager. Without any indication that rookie speedster Demond Claiborne will earn a bigger role, the Vikings could turn to Kenneth Gainwell, who has fallen out of favor in Tampa Bay. Safety is clearly the weak spot on an otherwise elite defense, with Harrison Smith very much looking his age and Joshua Metellus consistently on the wrong end of big plays. stories.title: Missed tackles hurt the Texas defense vs. Florida
stories.summary: The Longhorns missed 19 tackles against the Gators.
stories.detailText: AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 17: London Montgomery #24 of the Florida Gators and TJ Abrams #4 celebrate after defeating the Texas Longhorns at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images AUSTIN — Missed tackles played a significant role in the Texas Longhorns defense allowing a touchdown prior to halftime and suffering through the Florida Gators running 46 plays for 170 yards and 17 points during 21:51 of possession in the second half of Saturday’s 27-24 upset in Austin. According to Texas fifth-year defensive tackle Hero Kanu, the Horns missed 19 tackles in the loss, contributing to the Gators averaging 2.98 yards after contact per rush in gaining 134 of their 173 rushing yards after contact (77.5 percent) and 94 of their 155 receiving yards after the catch (60.6 percent), according to Pro Football Focus. Kanu called the missed tackles the most disappointing aspect of the defense’s performance. “We can’t allow it. That wasn’t even, let’s say, them [doing] a good job, but us just missing our leverage, leaving our feet, not driving on the tackle, and we’ve just got to fix those,” Kanu said. In an effort to improve against No. 7 Ole Miss on Saturday, Texas defenders spent an extra 10 to 15 minutes working a tackling circuit following Monday’s practice. “We know what we’ve got to get better at, and it’s going to be fixed,” Kanu said. The issues started in earnest on Florida’s touchdown drive before halftime. On the first play of the drive, a jet sweep to wide receiver Eric Singleton Jr. out-leveraged the Texas defense, but senior cornerback Bo Mascoe did a nice job of beating his blocker, he just couldn’t get the speedy Singleton to the ground near the line of scrimmage, leading to a gain of eight yards. After the Gators converted 4th and 12 with a 17-yard reception by wide receiver Dallas Wilson, quarterback Tramell Jones made the Longhorns pay with his legs, breaking a tackle attempt by senior linebacker Rasheem Biles in the backfield and another tackle attempt by junior safety Kobe Black down field to gain 14 yards to the Texas 5-yard line, setting up a seven-yard touchdown pass two plays later. Out of halftime, Florida mounted a 15-play, 69-yard drive that took 8:03 off the clock, beginning to severely tax the Texas defense. Several missed tackles contributed to that touchdown drive, but a missed call also loomed large when Kanu was tackled by a Gators offensive lineman as he tried to sack Jones on 2nd and 7 on the fifth play of the drive, allowing a four-yard scramble when the Florida quarterback picked up several yards after contact because junior edge Colin Simmons tried to force a fumble instead of wrapping up. Facing 3rd and 3, Florida was able to throw a screen pass to wide receiver Bailey Stockton that gained a fresh set of downs when sophomore cornerback Graceson Littleton’s fundamentals let him down — needing to run through Stockton’s outside hip to make the play, a hesitation move caused Littleton to break down, allowing Stockton to stiff arm Littleton on his tackle attempt, ultimately leading to the blown coverage on 3rd and 3 that resulted in Florida’s eight-yard touchdown pass . After the Longhorns forced a three and out on the next drive by the Gators, Florida went 57 yards on 14 plays over 6:31 to kick a 28-yard field goal early in the fourth quarter to take a 20-17 lead. A missed assignment by Black, who was responsible for covering Florida running back Jaden Baugh out of the backfield on 3rd and 3 near midfield to start the fourth quarter was a big blow on the drive, as Baugh gained 14 yards on the play, tied for the team’s second-longest completion on the day. Texas had a chance to get off the field on another 3rd and 3, but freshman edge Richard Wesley and sophomore defensive end Lance Jackson both missed tackle attempts on Baugh in the backfield, allowing a first down. On the next play, Littleton came free off the edge on a play-action pass and had a chance to inflict a major negative play eight yards behind the line of scrimmage, but Jones broke the tackle to run for a three-yard gain. Florida picked up more extra yardage on a trick play to running back London Montgomery, who spun out of a tackle attempt by McDonald to gain eight yards and a first down. A good open-field tackle of Singleton by sophomore cornerback Kade Phillips and strong coverage on two incompletions thrown by Jones allowed the Longhorns to finally get off the field in the red zone, but the inability to get Baugh to the ground ensured the Gators could kick a short field goal and forced the defense to spend five more plays on the field while taking close to three minutes off the clock. The inability to play complementary football hurt the Texas defense on Florida’s next drive, which started inside Longhorns territory after a turnover on downs. Senior linebacker Justin Cryer lost his leverage on Baugh when the Gator running back ran into an offensive lineman in the backfield before taking the edge for a 13-yard gain. A bad angle by Cryer on the next play led to a nine-yard run with several yards after contact. Tasked with scrape exchanging on a zone read by Jones, Cryer had his eyes wrong and was late to react, allowing a nine-yard gain from the high red zone and setting up Baugh’s 11-yard touchdown run when Black lost leverage running the alley and Baugh took advantage, taking the edge and scoring. Missed tackles weren’t really an issue on that drive, but spending so much time on the field in the second half might have contributed to some of the mental breakdowns as the Gators took a 10-point lead. A fumbled snap by Jones on first down put Florida behind the chains on its next drive, another three and out, but the tackling issues resurfaced following quarterback Arch Manning’s fumble as the Gators were able to pick up the first down necessary to finish the game in victory formation. Baugh started the drive by squeezing through the pile to gain two yards after contact, picked up another yard after contact on second down, then Jones kept a zone read, running behind a missed holding call against Texas senior edge Brad Spence before making McDonald look bad in the open field on a nine-yard gain that sealed the victory. The missed tackles weren’t the only problem for Texas defensively as Florida scored 24 points on its final seven drives, including too many easy-access throws and breakdowns in fundamentals, but the inability to get Gators to the ground was a huge factor in the loss.

McCarthy against the Texans on Sunday. McCarthy will replace Jameis Winston, who started the last four games and helped the Giants to a 2-1-1 record. The one loss came against New Orleans last weekend and Winston was benched after throwing two interceptions. McCarthy led the Giants to 17 points in the fourth quarter of the 34-27 loss and the team will now see if he can produce at that level over a full game. Harbaugh said the decision was based on "what gives us the best chance to play the best offense we can." Harbaugh noted that unforeseen circumstances often crop up, but said that he does not plan to revisit the decision on a weekly basis "Life is day-to-day, minute-to-minute ," Harbaugh said, via SNY. "There's really no guarantees. I would never say that anything is permanent in football or life. That's the plan going forward." McCarthy joined the Giants in a trade with the Vikings a few weeks ago, but Harbaugh feels he had the game plan down "pretty fully" last Sunday and that it will be more tailored to McCarthy's direction now that the team has decided to make a change. If all goes well, it will remain that way for the rest of the year and McCarthy will consistently show the ability that made him a first-round pick in 2024.

stories.detailText: FOXBOROUGH, MA - OCTOBER 11: Alijah Vera-Tucker #75 of the New England Patriots during a game between the New England Patriots and the Las Vegas Raiders on October 11, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New England Patriots will be down both starting guards at Soldier Field. Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown have been ruled out for Thursday night’s matchup against the Chicago Bears, as head coach Mike Vrabel announced during his final press conference of the short week. A hamstring injury and a knee injury , respectively, kept the two offensive linemen sidelined throughout preparations. Cornerbacks Carlton Davis III, Karon Prunty and Channing Canada will also be missing in the Midwest, while four members of the active roster stand as questionable. Here’s the rest of the game statuses leading up to the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff. OUT Patriots G Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) G Ben Brown (knee) CB Carlton Davis III (neck) CB Karon Prunty (hamstring) CB Channing Canada (hamstring) Bears RB Kyle Monangai (thumb, toe) LB Jack Sanborn (concussion) New England’s left guard and right guard had been ruled out on the way to what became a 26-19 win last Sunday. The musical chairs sent Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse in along the interior. No sacks nor penalties followed for what remained of the front five against the New York Jets. The October signing as well as the August trade acquisition that stepped in for 46 and 14 offensive downs, respectively, are now set to start over the shoulders of center Jared Wilson . There were three cornerbacks among the inactives for the AFC East meeting at Gillette Stadium. And despite recently returning as a limited participant , the Patriots’ secondary will be again without Davis for a third consecutive game. The veteran outside starter has dealt with a neck issue dating back to September and had missed the previous two full weeks of practice. That leaves 2025 waiver claim Charles Woods and team captain Marcus Jones on deck for expanded roles alongside All-Pro Christian Gonzalez. Hamstring injuries will also keep a pair of rookies who have combined for 76 snaps on special teams out for Thursday night. DOUBTFUL Patriots No players listed Bears LB T.J. Edwards (hamstring) No Patriots check in with a doubtful designation, but the Bears will likely be without two linebackers under the lights at Soldier Field after one was already ruled out. The doubtful Edwards was a partial participant on Wednesday while working through a hamstring injury. He stands with 16 tackles and one interception through five starts this fall for Chicago’s front. QUESTIONABLE Patriots OT Morgan Moses (foot) LB Christian Elliss (chest) S Kevin Byard III (chest) S Craig Woodson (shoulder) Bears CB Tyrique Stevenson Sr. (hip) The lone questionable Patriot not to practice in full on kickoff’s eve was Moses, who has been listed as limited since the initial estimation . The 35-year-old captain had exited just nine offensive downs into last weekend’s start at right tackle. In his absence due to a foot injury, rookie No. 28 overall pick Caleb Lomu went from reporting as an eligible tight end to stepping in as the bookend opposite blindside starter Will Campbell. New England could elect to activate swing tackle Marcus Bryant from injured reserve before Thursday’s 4 p.m. ET deadline for roster moves. The 2025 seventh-rounder’s 21-day practice window opened midway through October. He has since ramped up to full participation as well as no game designation. With two offensive linemen officially ruled out, the 53-man roster currently includes seven options available. The organization brought back blockers Jacob Rizy and Andrew Rupcich on the practice squad amid the attrition.

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are 3-3 and need to make a move to give not only the offense, but the team a shot in the arm. In previous weeks, the chatter centered on Marvin Harrison Jr., Brian Thomas Jr., and any other wide receiver. However, there is a need that will fix far more than just the passing game. Carlie Irsay-Gordon, the owner of the Indianapolis Colts fired her general manager of 10 years, Chris Ballard. Many speculate an oncoming fire sale as the Colts look to potentially dump salary and begin the tear down phase of a rebuild. One of the players rumored to be available is Guard Quenton Nelson. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak has cited a need to get better production across the offensive line. Nelson is 30 years old, an 8-time Pro Bowler and a 6-time All-Pro. Nelson has the unique set of skills that can make the entire offense better overnight. Instant impact With Nelson, the run blocking becomes 20% better and takes some of the stress off center Tyler Linderbaum, so he can focus on his blocking assignment instead of being a help blocker. Maybe even help him out so that running backs stop getting hit in the backfield. Combine that with a switch to Mike Washington Jr. as the number one back and suddenly the Raiders are controlling the clock on the ground, allowing the defense to rest and not be overextended. Against the Buffalo Bills in the waning moments of the game, we saw a beautiful deep ball to Tre Tucker who came up with a diving catch in the end zone. Nelson’s pass blocking provides interior protection for the quarterbacks, be it Kirk Cousins now and/or Fernando Mendoza later. Giving receivers more time to get open and get deep, making all of the existing pass catchers better. The fallout Kubiak may profess a healthy respect for Spencer Burford but we can be honest in this safe space. Burford has been a liability. There is not good, and there is what Burford has been. For someone with experience in Kubiak’s system it’s inexcusable how he isn’t obtaining larger amounts of success. Nelson erases that issue outright, helps both Kolton Miller and Linderbaum. Potentially allows for Trey Zuhn to be slid out to left tackle, if need be and keeps continuity in the better performing right side of the line. The question is, what will it cost? Would the Colts be interested in a cheaper veteran cornerback such as Eric Stokes and a second- or third-round draft pick? If so, the deal should be done posthaste. Or perhaps a young defensive end like Malcolm Koonce? That’s where the Raiders general manager John Spytek will have to be willing to make a splash that will help his team for years to come.

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are beginning he practice week for Sunday’s home game against the Los Angeles Rams without starting defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said the 2025 fourth-round is still in the NFL’s concussion protocol. He was hurt in Week 5 and he didn’t play in a Week 6 loss to the Buffalo Bills. Monday, Kubiak said he was expecting Hemingway back in practice this week. If he returns to practice by Friday, he can still have a chance to face the Rams. Hemingway has been the Raiders’ snap leader at defensive tackle. He averaged playing 62 percent of the snaps in the four games he was fully healthy for. Foley Fatukasi started in place of Hemingway against the Bills. Meanwhile, Kubiak said second-year wide receiver Dont’e Thornton has a chance to be activated from the injured reserve this week, but the coach indicated Thornton has to show he’s ready. He must be activated by next week or he would be out for the season. Kubiak also said there will be compettion on the offensive line again this week. teamStories.detailText: The 3-3 Las Vegas Raiders host the 2-4 Los Angeles Rams on Sunday at Allegiant Stadium. Kickoff is 1:25 p.m. PT. Here are some things to consider about the Rams: They can move the ball: The Rams have their problems, but the numbers say they are doing some things right. They have outgained their opponents by 644 yards this season. That’s an average of 107.3 yards a game. That is a testament to both sides of the ball. It shows the Rams are playing well in some areas. They’re losing close games: In their last three losses, the Rams have been outscored by a total of nine points with the biggest deficit being four points. They are 2-4 with a total points deficit of three points. Defensive line decimated: In addition to playing with starting wide receiver, former Raider, Davante Adams, the Rams’ defensive front, an expected NFL force, has been ravaged by injuries. They are without star defensive end Myles Garrett and standout defensive tackle Poona Ford and Kobie Turner. The Raiders might be able to get the ground game going Sunday. Aaron Donald snap counts: With Turner and Ford out, Aaron Donald may see more playing time. He has averaged playing 58.6 percent of the Rams’ defensive snaps in the four games he has played this season after he returned from retiring for the past two seasons. So the Raiders may see a lot of the 35-year-old future Hall of Famer. New quarterbacks coming: While this game will feature veteran quarterbacks Matthew Stafford and Kirk Cousins, the next time these two teams play will likely feature 2026 first-round picks Fernando Mendoza and Ty Simpson, the No. 1 and No. 13 overall draft picks. Both players did well in the preseason. Mendoza has mopped up in one game, while Simpson hasn’t played this season.
